4.4.0.m: Having filled the vessel for clarified butter and the dipping spoon with curds, having drawn near the chair, holding plants in their hands, they cleanse themselves at the cātvāla with [the mantra], "Homage to speech!"

4.4.0.s: yadi mahāvīra upadasyet pra vāṃ dam̐sām̐si \\ ity upadasta āpyāyyamānaḥ /
4.4.0.d: यदि महावीर उपदस्येत् प्र वां दम्̐साम्̐सि \\ इत्य् उपदस्त आप्याय्यमानः /
4.4.0.m: If the mahāvīra [pot] should fail [in contents], with [the verse], "Forth your wondrous powers…," [the pot] is restored while it has failed.

4.4.0.s: yadi mahāvīro bhidyeta mā no gharma hvaritas \\ ity etābhyāṃ pratyṛcam āhutīr juhuyād vyāhṛtibhiś ca /
4.4.0.d: यदि महावीरो भिद्येत मा नो घर्म ह्वरितस् \\ इत्य् एताभ्यां प्रत्यृचम् आहुतीर् जुहुयाद् व्याहृतिभिश् च /
4.4.0.m: If the mahāvīra [pot] should break, he should offer oblations verse by verse with the two [verses beginning with], "May not the gharma, crooked, [harm] us," and with the sacred utterances.

4.4.0.s: vyākhyātaṃ karaṇam //
4.4.0.d: व्याख्यातं करणम् //

4.4.0.s: gharmaḥ śiras \\ iti yathākālaṃ gharmeṣṭakām upadadhāti //
4.4.0.d: घर्मः शिरस् \\ इति यथाकालं घर्मेष्टकाम् उपदधाति //
4.4.0.m: With [the formula], "The gharma is the head," he lays down the gharmeṣṭakā brick at the proper time.

4.4.0.s: pūṣṇa āghṛṇaye svāhā \\ iti yathākālam̐ svayam eva pañcāhutīr juhoti //
4.4.0.d: पूष्ण आघृणये स्वाहा \\ इति यथाकालम्̐ स्वयम् एव पञ्चाहुतीर् जुहोति //
4.4.0.m: With [the formula], "To the glowing Pūṣan, hail!", he himself offers five oblations at the proper time.

4.4.0.s: ugraś ca bhīmaś ca \\ iti yathākālam araṇye 'nuvākyo gaṇo gaṇaḥ /
4.4.0.d: उग्रश् च भीमश् च \\ इति यथाकालम् अरण्ये ऽनुवाक्यो गणो गणः /
4.4.0.m: The troop [of mantras] beginning with "The fierce and the terrible" is to be recited in the forest at the proper time, troop by troop.

4.5.0.m: Now they proceed with the dadhigharma.

4.5.0.s: mādhyaṃdine savane grahān saṃmṛśyopayāmaṃ darbhaiḥ prakṣālya paścād āgnīdhrīyasya gāyatrīṃ chandas \\ iti prapadyanta ṛtvijo yajamānaś ca //
4.5.0.d: माध्यंदिने सवने ग्रहान् संमृश्योपयामं दर्भैः प्रक्षाल्य पश्चाद् आग्नीध्रीयस्य गायत्रीं छन्दस् \\ इति प्रपद्यन्त ऋत्विजो यजमानश् च //
4.5.0.m: At the midday pressing, having touched the cups, having washed the upayāma vessel with darbha grass, behind the āgnīdhra's fire the officiating priests and the sacrificer enter with [the formula], "Gāyatrī is the metre…"

4.5.0.s: hotar vadasva \\ ity uktvā jyotir asi \\ ity upayāme dadhy ānīya śrātam̐ haviḥ śrātaṃ devebhyas \\ iti preṣyati //
4.5.0.d: होतर् वदस्व \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा ज्योतिर् असि \\ इत्य् उपयामे दध्य् आनीय श्रातम्̐ हविः श्रातं देवेभ्यस् \\ इति प्रेष्यति //
4.5.0.m: Having said, "Speak, O hotṛ!", and having poured curd into the support-vessel with "You are light...", he prompts: "The oblation is cooked! Cooked for the gods!"

4.5.0.s: yadi śrāto juhotana \ yady aśrāto mamattana \\ iti śrutvā sthānaṃ gatvāśrāvayati /
4.5.0.d: यदि श्रातो जुहोतन \ यद्य् अश्रातो ममत्तन \\ इति श्रुत्वा स्थानं गत्वाश्रावयति /
4.5.0.m: Having heard, "If it is cooked, offer it! If it is not cooked, exhilarate!", having gone to his station, he causes the call to be made.
When the response has been made, he prompts: "Recite the offering verse for the curd-Gharma!"

4.5.0.s: yam indram iti pratinigadya vaṣaṭkṛte na sarvaṃ juhoti // tābhyām̐ svāhā vaṣaḍ ity anuvaṣaṭkṛte /
4.5.0.d: यम् इन्द्रम् इति प्रतिनिगद्य वषट्कृते न सर्वं जुहोति // ताभ्याम्̐ स्वाहा वषड् इत्य् अनुवषट्कृते /
4.5.0.m: Having recited the response with "yam indram...", when the vaṣaṭ-call is uttered, he does not sacrifice all [of it]. When the second vaṣaṭ-call is uttered with "tābhyāṃ svāhā vaṣaṭ",
he takes the portion for consumption in the upayāma [ladle].

4.5.0.s: sado gatvā \\ upahūtopahvayasva \\ ity uktvā \\ upahūtā upahvayadhvam iti vā //
4.5.0.d: सदो गत्वा \\ उपहूतोपह्वयस्व \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा \\ उपहूता उपह्वयध्वम् इति वा //
4.5.0.m: Going to the sadas and saying, "Summoned, do you invite [me]!" or "Summoned, do you invite [us]!"

4.5.0.s: bhūr bhuvaḥ svar \ mayi tyad iti bhakṣayanti /
4.5.0.d: भूर् भुवः स्वर् \ मयि त्यद् इति भक्षयन्ति /
4.5.0.m: they consume [it] with: "bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ; mayi tyad..."

4.5.0.s: gharmam upayāmaṃ mārjālīye darbhaiḥ prakṣālya dadhnā pūrayitvā \\ udasya śuṣmād ity āhavanīya ādadhāti /
4.5.0.d: घर्मम् उपयामं मार्जालीये दर्भैः प्रक्षाल्य दध्ना पूरयित्वा \\ उदस्य शुष्माद् इत्य् आहवनीय आदधाति /
4.5.0.m: Having washed the gharma [pot] and the upayāma [ladle] at the mārjālīya with darbha grass and filled [them] with curd, he places [the pot] on the āhavanīya fire with "udasya śuṣmāt..."

4.5.0.s: namo vāce \\ ity oṣadhipāṇayaś cātvālānte mārjayante /
4.5.0.d: नमो वाचे \\ इत्य् ओषधिपाणयश् चात्वालान्ते मार्जयन्ते /
4.5.0.m: With "namo vāce...", holding plants in their hands, they sprinkle themselves at the edge of the cātvāla trench.

4.6.0.s: vijre vikṣipe vidhame \\ iti tisro vijra ehi \\ ity aṣṭau /
4.6.0.d: विज्रे विक्षिपे विधमे \\ इति तिस्रो विज्र एहि \\ इत्य् अष्टौ /
4.6.0.m: [There are] three [verses beginning with] "vijre vikṣipe vidhame..." and eight [verses beginning with] "vijra ehi..."

4.6.0.s: yaṃ dviṣyāt tasya gavāṃ madhye vijre vikṣipe vidhame \\ ity āhūya prāgudayān niṣkramya dakṣiṇato grāmasya paścād vā śucau deśe svakṛta iriṇe 'gniṃ prajvālya kṛṣṇāyāḥ kṛṣṇānām̐ vrīhīṇām̐ payasi sthālīpākam̐ śrapayitvā / tasminn upasamādhāya parisamuhya paryukṣya śaraiḥ paristīrya \\ asṛṅmukhas \\ iti sthālīpākasya hutvā / prāk sviṣṭakṛtaḥ śarabhṛṣṭinā dakṣiṇasyoror deśasya savyam asyāṅge dakṣiṇā niḥkāsya sthalam /
4.6.0.d: यं द्विष्यात् तस्य गवां मध्ये विज्रे विक्षिपे विधमे \\ इत्य् आहूय प्रागुदयान् निष्क्रम्य दक्षिणतो ग्रामस्य पश्चाद् वा शुचौ देशे स्वकृत इरिणे ऽग्निं प्रज्वाल्य कृष्णायाः कृष्णानाम्̐ व्रीहीणाम्̐ पयसि स्थालीपाकम्̐ श्रपयित्वा / तस्मिन्न् उपसमाधाय परिसमुह्य पर्युक्ष्य शरैः परिस्तीर्य \\ असृङ्मुखस् \\ इति स्थालीपाकस्य हुत्वा / प्राक् स्विष्टकृतः शरभृष्टिना दक्षिणस्योरोर् देशस्य सव्यम् अस्याङ्गे दक्षिणा निःकास्य स्थलम् /
4.6.0.m: Having called out in the midst of the cows of one whom he hates, "vijre vikṣipe vidhame...", going out before sunrise to the south or west of the village, in a clean place, having kindled a fire in a naturally formed barren spot, having cooked a boiled pot-oblation of black rice in the milk of a black cow; having added fuel to that [fire], swept around, sprinkled around, and strewn around with reeds, having offered of the boiled pot-oblation with "asṛṅmukhaḥ...", before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, [piercing] with the point of a reed the left side in the body of a [clay] figure [placed] south of the region of the right thigh, having scraped out [the residue],

4.6.0.s: vṛkṣam āruhya grāmaṃ nagaraṃ janapadam̐ vā yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ dhruvor ity avekṣeta sa sadyo vinaśyati //
4.6.0.d: वृक्षम् आरुह्य ग्रामं नगरं जनपदम्̐ वा यं द्विष्यात् तं ध्रुवोर् इत्य् अवेक्षेत स सद्यो विनश्यति //
4.6.0.m: having climbed a tree, he should look towards the village, town, or country of him whom he hates, with "dhruvoḥ..."; he perishes immediately.

4.6.0.s: ud vayaṃ tamasas pari \\ ity ādityam avekṣate /
4.6.0.d: उद् वयं तमसस् परि \\ इत्य् आदित्यम् अवेक्षते /
4.6.0.m: He looks at the sun with "ud vayaṃ tamasas pari..."

4.6.0.s: pratyetya namo vāce \\ ity oṣadhipāṇir mārjayate mārjayate /
4.6.0.d: प्रत्येत्य नमो वाचे \\ इत्य् ओषधिपाणिर् मार्जयते मार्जयते /
4.6.0.m: Returning, holding a plant in his hand, he sprinkles himself with "namo vāce..."

4.7.0.s: avāntaradīkṣām upaiṣyann udagayane jyautsne puṇye nakṣatre 'nyatra navamyāḥ prāg astamayān niṣkramyottarato grāmasya purastād vā śucau deśe 'hatena vāsasā pariṇaddhaḥ sarvarātraṃ tiṣṭhet strīśūdram anabhibhāṣamāṇaḥ /
4.7.0.d: अवान्तरदीक्षाम् उपैष्यन्न् उदगयने ज्यौत्स्ने पुण्ये नक्षत्रे ऽन्यत्र नवम्याः प्राग् अस्तमयान् निष्क्रम्योत्तरतो ग्रामस्य पुरस्ताद् वा शुचौ देशे ऽहतेन वाससा परिणद्धः सर्वरात्रं तिष्ठेत् स्त्रीशूद्रम् अनभिभाषमाणः /
4.7.0.m: When about to undertake the intermediate consecration during the northern course of the sun, in the bright fortnight, under an auspicious lunar mansion, except on the ninth day, having gone out before sunset to the north or east of the village, wrapped in an unwashed garment in a clean place, he should stand all night without speaking to a woman or a Śūdra.

4.7.0.s: śvobhūte 'gnim̐ sūryaṃ gām̐ hiraṇyaṃ brāhmaṇam udakām̐syaṃ ca kanyāṃ patikāmām iti nidarśayet /
4.7.0.d: श्वोभूते ऽग्निम्̐ सूर्यं गाम्̐ हिरण्यं ब्राह्मणम् उदकाम्̐स्यं च कन्यां पतिकामाम् इति निदर्शयेत् /
4.7.0.m: On the next day, he should display fire, the sun, a cow, gold, a brāhmaṇa, a bronze vessel of water, and a maiden desiring a husband.

4.7.0.s: tatraivāgnim upasamādhāya caityasyāśvatthasyārdrāś catasraḥ samidhaḥ stibhigavatīḥ sahapalāśāḥ prādeśamātrīḥ sarpiṣi paryastāḥ pṛthivī samid iti svāhākārāntābhir ādadhāti //
4.7.0.d: तत्रैवाग्निम् उपसमाधाय चैत्यस्याश्वत्थस्यार्द्राश् चतस्रः समिधः स्तिभिगवतीः सहपलाशाः प्रादेशमात्रीः सर्पिषि पर्यस्ताः पृथिवी समिद् इति स्वाहाकारान्ताभिर् आदधाति //
4.7.0.m: Having added fuel to the fire right there, he places on [it] four moist firewood sticks from a caitya-aśvattha tree, possessing shoots, with leaves, a span in length, soaked in clarified butter, with the [formulas] ending in svāhā: "pṛthivī samit..."

4.7.0.s: agne vratapate \\ iti vrataṃ pradāyāditaḥ pañcavim̐śatim anuvākān anuvācayet /
4.7.0.d: अग्ने व्रतपते \\ इति व्रतं प्रदायादितः पञ्चविम्̐शतिम् अनुवाकान् अनुवाचयेत् /
4.7.0.m: Having imparted the vow with "agne vratapate...", he should have him recite the twenty-five sections from the beginning.

4.7.0.s: pariṇahanaṃ gāṃ kām̐syaṃ ca gurave dadyāt /
4.7.0.d: परिणहनं गां काम्̐स्यं च गुरवे दद्यात् /
4.7.0.m: He should give the wrap, a cow, and a bronze vessel to the teacher.

4.7.0.s: na naktaṃ bhuñjīta / yadi bhuñjītāpajvalitaṃ bhuñjīta /
4.7.0.d: न नक्तं भुञ्जीत / यदि भुञ्जीतापज्वलितं भुञ्जीत /
4.7.0.m: He should not eat at night. If he should eat, he should eat by the light of a flame.

4.7.0.s: ahas tiṣṭhed rātrāv āsīnaḥ / parvasu caivam̐ syāt /
4.7.0.d: अहस् तिष्ठेद् रात्राव् आसीनः / पर्वसु चैवम्̐ स्यात् /
4.7.0.m: He should stand by day, seated at night. And it should be thus on the new- and full-moon days.

4.7.0.s: evam̐yuktaḥ sam̐vatsaraṃ caret trīn pañca sapta vā / traividyakaṃ ca caret /
4.7.0.d: एवम्̐युक्तः सम्̐वत्सरं चरेत् त्रीन् पञ्च सप्त वा / त्रैविद्यकं च चरेत् /
4.7.0.m: Engaged in this way, he should observe it for a year, or three, five, or seven [years]. And he should observe the study of the three Vedas.

4.7.0.s: samāpte ca tāny utsṛjya namo vāce \\ ity oṣadhipāṇir mārjayate mārjayate /
4.7.0.d: समाप्ते च तान्य् उत्सृज्य नमो वाचे \\ इत्य् ओषधिपाणिर् मार्जयते मार्जयते /
4.7.0.m: And when it is completed, having relinquished them, holding a plant in his hand, he sprinkles himself with "namo vāce..."

4.8.0.s: āraṇyam̐ svādhyāyam adhyeṣyamāṇa udagayane jyautsne śukriyaṃ pūrvāhṇe na naktaṃ na bhuktvā na yāme na śoṇitaṃ dṛṣṭvāmam̐ vā mām̐sam anyad vāmedhyaṃ parvasu ca partiṣiddham /
4.8.0.d: आरण्यम्̐ स्वाध्यायम् अध्येष्यमाण उदगयने ज्यौत्स्ने शुक्रियं पूर्वाह्णे न नक्तं न भुक्त्वा न यामे न शोणितं दृष्ट्वामम्̐ वा माम्̐सम् अन्यद् वामेध्यं पर्वसु च पर्तिषिद्धम् /
4.8.0.m: When about to study the forest lesson, in the northern course of the sun, in the bright fortnight, [he studies] the Śukriya [text] in the morning, not at night, not after eating, not at a forbidden watch [of the day], not after seeing blood, raw meat, or anything else impure, and it is prohibited on the new- and full-moon days;

4.8.0.s: prāg udayān niṣkramyottarato grāmasya purastād vā śucau deśe viṣṭarapāṇayo 'bhimukhās tad anucakṣuṣo yathākālam̐ svādhyāyam adhītya namo vāce \\ ity oṣadhipāṇayo mārjayante /
4.8.0.d: प्राग् उदयान् निष्क्रम्योत्तरतो ग्रामस्य पुरस्ताद् वा शुचौ देशे विष्टरपाणयो ऽभिमुखास् तद् अनुचक्षुषो यथाकालम्̐ स्वाध्यायम् अधीत्य नमो वाचे \\ इत्य् ओषधिपाणयो मार्जयन्ते /
4.8.0.m: having gone out before sunrise to the north or east of the village, in a clean place, holding grass bunches in their hands, facing [the sun], with eyes fixed upon that [text], having studied the sacred text according to the proper time, holding plants in their hands, they sprinkle themselves with "namo vāce..."

4.8.0.s: sarvatra rahasyamantraprayoge pratipattir mārjanaṃ ca pratipattir mārjanaṃ ca /
4.8.0.d: सर्वत्र रहस्यमन्त्रप्रयोगे प्रतिपत्तिर् मार्जनं च प्रतिपत्तिर् मार्जनं च /
4.8.0.m: Everywhere in the application of secret formulas, [there is] disposal and sprinkling, disposal and sprinkling.

5.1.1.s: iṣṭibhir yajeta paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyām̐ vā pūrvapakṣe vā puṇye nakṣatre 'nyatra navamyāḥ /
5.1.1.d: इष्टिभिर् यजेत पौर्णमास्याम् अमावास्यायाम्̐ वा पूर्वपक्षे वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे ऽन्यत्र नवम्याः /
5.1.1.m: One should sacrifice with iṣṭis on a full-moon day, or on a new-moon day, or in the bright fortnight under an auspicious lunar mansion, except on the ninth day.
An expiatory iṣṭi occurs at a time of emergency; one should perform it immediately.

5.1.1.s: tūṣṇīm agniṣv anvādhāya vratam upaity anyatra niyatakālābhyaḥ samṛtayajñāc ca /
5.1.1.d: तूष्णीम् अग्निष्व् अन्वाधाय व्रतम् उपैत्य् अन्यत्र नियतकालाभ्यः समृतयज्ञाच् च /
5.1.1.m: Having added fuel silently to the fires, he enters upon the vow, except in those rites that have fixed times and except at a gathering-sacrifice.

5.1.1.s: āhavanīyotkarāv antarā tīrthaṃ cātvālotkarāv antarā sacātvālāsu /
5.1.1.d: आहवनीयोत्कराव् अन्तरा तीर्थं चात्वालोत्कराव् अन्तरा सचात्वालासु /
5.1.1.m: The path lies between the āhavanīya fire and the rubbish heap; in rites with a cātvāla trench, between the cātvāla trench and the rubbish heap.
Seventeen are the kindling verses.

5.1.1.s: pṛthupājās \ tam̐ sabādhas \\ iti pṛthupājavatyau dhāyye / samidvatyāvantarā dhāyyāsthānam /
5.1.1.d: पृथुपाजास् \ तम्̐ सबाधस् \\ इति पृथुपाजवत्यौ धाय्ये / समिद्वत्यावन्तरा धाय्यास्थानम् /
5.1.1.m: "pṛthupājāḥ..." and "taṃ sabādhaḥ..." are the two inserting verses containing the word pṛthupājas; the place of the inserting verses is between the two [verses] containing the word samidh.
The insertion of the deities to be worshipped is between the clarified butter portion and the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.1.s: nigadamāvāhana uttame prayāje sviṣṭakṛti sūktavāke ca /
5.1.1.d: निगदमावाहन उत्तमे प्रयाजे स्विष्टकृति सूक्तवाके च /
5.1.1.m: [Their] invocation [occurs] in the invitation-formula, in the last fore-offering, in the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, and in the sūktavāka recitation.

5.1.1.s: avyavahitāḥ samānadevatāḥ sakṛd āvapet pratīcyam̐ vyavahitāḥ /
5.1.1.d: अव्यवहिताः समानदेवताः सकृद् आवपेत् प्रतीच्यम्̐ व्यवहिताः /
5.1.1.m: He should insert consecutive [names of deities] having the same divinity once; [names that are] separated, towards the end [of each].

5.1.1.s: paśupuroḍāśam̐ yāni cānvāyatante trimātrāṇi bhavati // ye3 yajāmahe \\ ādir \ ehi \\ āvaha \\ iti co śrāvaya \\ ity ādito dve brūhipreṣyaśrauṣaḍvauṣaṭsūpottamam̐ yājyāntaś ca / tasmin saṃdhyakṣarāṇy apragṛhyāṇi vivekena plavante /
5.1.1.d: पशुपुरोडाशम्̐ यानि चान्वायतन्ते त्रिमात्राणि भवति // ये3 यजामहे \\ आदिर् \ एहि \\ आवह \\ इति चो श्रावय \\ इत्य् आदितो द्वे ब्रूहिप्रेष्यश्रौषड्वौषट्सूपोत्तमम्̐ याज्यान्तश् च / तस्मिन् संध्यक्षराण्य् अप्रगृह्याणि विवेकेन प्लवन्ते /
5.1.1.m: The animal cake and whatever [syllables] follow become protracted to three morae: the beginning of "ye3 yajāmahe", "ehi" and "āvaha", the first two of "oṃ śrāvaya", the penultimate [syllables] in "brūhi", "preṣya", "vauṣaṭ", and the end of the offering verse; in that, diphthongs that are not pragṛhya become protracted distinctly.

5.1.1.s: śastrānuvacanayor uttamam akṣaram̐ svarādy okārī bhavati /
5.1.1.d: शस्त्रानुवचनयोर् उत्तमम् अक्षरम्̐ स्वराद्य् ओकारी भवति /
5.1.1.m: In the recitation of a śastra and the reciting of a text, the final syllable, beginning with a vowel, turns into an o-sound.
In an aggregate of verses, [he repeats] the first and the last three times.
He connects the verses with the praṇava [om].
In the iṣṭis of the establishment of the sacred fires, the introductory offering is to be performed as a subsidiary offering.
In the Anīkavat, Sāṃtapana, and Krīḍin [offerings], fifteen are the kindling verses.

5.1.1.s: rājanyāśrivadhryaśvavasiṣṭhavaiśyaśunakānāṃ kaṇvakaśyapasaṃkṛtīnāṃ narāśam̐so dvitīyaḥ prayājas tanūnapād anyeṣām ubhau yatra samāmnātau /
5.1.1.d: राजन्याश्रिवध्र्यश्ववसिष्ठवैश्यशुनकानां कण्वकश्यपसंकृतीनां नराशम्̐सो द्वितीयः प्रयाजस् तनूनपाद् अन्येषाम् उभौ यत्र समाम्नातौ /
5.1.1.m: For royal seers, the Avadhryāśvas, Vasiṣṭhas, Vaiśyas, and Śunakas, and for the Kaṇvas, Kaśyapas, and Saṃkṛtis, Narāśaṃsa is the second fore-offering; Tanūnapāt is for others; where both are handed down by tradition, [both are used].

5.1.1.s: yasyai devatāyai vaṣaṭkuryāt tāṃ manasā dhyāyet /
5.1.1.d: यस्यै देवतायै वषट्कुर्यात् तां मनसा ध्यायेत् /
5.1.1.m: To whichever deity he would utter the vaṣaṭ-call, he should meditate upon that [deity] in his mind.
One who desires heaven should sacrifice with an offering on eight potsherds to Agni according to the ritual framework of the full-moon sacrifice.

5.1.1.s: agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat \ tvam̐ somāsi satpatir iti vārtraghnāv ājyabhāgau //
5.1.1.d: अग्निर् वृत्राणि जङ्घनत् \ त्वम्̐ सोमासि सत्पतिर् इति वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्यभागौ //
5.1.1.m: "agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat..." and "tvaṃ somāsi satpatiḥ..." are the two clarified butter portions celebrating the slaying of Vṛtra.

5.1.1.s: agnir mūrdhā \ bhuvo yajñasya \\ iti haviṣaḥ //
5.1.1.d: अग्निर् मूर्धा \ भुवो यज्ञस्य \\ इति हविषः //
5.1.1.m: "agnir mūrdhā..." and "bhuvo yajñasya..." are [the invitatory and offering verses] of the oblation.

5.1.1.s: piprīhi devān \ agne yad adya \\ iti sviṣṭakṛtaḥ sam̐yājye /
5.1.1.d: पिप्रीहि देवान् \ अग्ने यद् अद्य \\ इति स्विष्टकृतः सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.1.m: "piprīhi devān..." and "agne yad adya..." are the two concluding offering verses of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
In the absence of an explicit rule, the ritual framework of the full-moon sacrifice [applies].

5.1.1.s: kapāle naṣṭe prayuktānāṃ prāg udvāsanād agnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet /
5.1.1.d: कपाले नष्टे प्रयुक्तानां प्राग् उद्वासनाद् अग्नये वैश्वानराय द्वादशकपालं निर्वपेत् /
5.1.1.m: When a potsherd among those used is lost before taking [the cake] off the fire, one should apportion an oblation on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara.
A one-year-old cow is the sacrificial gift.

5.1.1.s: agne rakṣā ṇas \ tvaṃ naḥ soma \\ iti rakṣitavantāv ājyabhāgau //
5.1.1.d: अग्ने रक्षा णस् \ त्वं नः सोम \\ इति रक्षितवन्ताव् आज्यभागौ //
5.1.1.m: "agne rakṣā ṇaḥ..." and "tvaṃ naḥ soma..." are the two clarified butter portions containing the word rakṣat.

5.1.1.s: vaiśvānaro na ūtyā \ pṛṣṭo divi \\ iti haviṣaḥ //
5.1.1.d: वैश्वानरो न ऊत्या \ पृष्टो दिवि \\ इति हविषः //
5.1.1.m: "vaiśvānaro na ūtyā..." and "pṛṣṭo divi..." are [the verses] of the oblation.

5.1.1.s: viśvāni nas \\ agne tvaṃ pārayā \\ iti pārayadvatyau sam̐yājye /
5.1.1.d: विश्वानि नस् \\ अग्ने त्वं पारया \\ इति पारयद्वत्यौ सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.1.m: "viśvāni naḥ..." and "agne tvaṃ pārayā..." are the two concluding offering verses containing the word pārayat.
In all introductory offerings, the ritual framework of the full-moon sacrifice [applies].
In the establishment of the sacred fires, the introductory offering has three oblations or four oblations.
"agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā..." are the six [verses] of that with three oblations.

5.1.1.s: tvam agne vīravat \ tvaṃ bhago nas \\ ity āgnāvaiṣṇavād anantare caturhaviṣaḥ /
5.1.1.d: त्वम् अग्ने वीरवत् \ त्वं भगो नस् \\ इत्य् आग्नावैष्णवाद् अनन्तरे चतुर्हविषः /
5.1.1.m: "tvam agne vīravat..." and "tvaṃ bhago naḥ..." immediately follow the [verses] to Agni-Viṣṇu for that with four oblations.
If [the sacrifice to] Bhaga is performed for a wish, it has a separate ritual framework.

5.1.1.s: agniḥ pratnena manmanā \ soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayam iti vṛdhanvantāv ājyabhāgau /
5.1.1.d: अग्निः प्रत्नेन मन्मना \ सोम गीर्भिष् ट्वा वयम् इति वृधन्वन्ताव् आज्यभागौ /
5.1.1.m: "Agni by ancient thought…", "O Soma, we [praise] you with songs…" are the two clarified butter portions containing the word vṛdh- [vṛdhanvant].
"Kindled, O Agni…" are the two virāj concluding offering verses.

5.1.2.s: agnyādheyeṣṭīnāṃ pavamānasya \\ agna āyūm̐ṣi pavase \\ iti dve haviṣa uttare sviṣṭakṛtaḥ //
5.1.2.d: अग्न्याधेयेष्टीनां पवमानस्य \\ अग्न आयूम्̐षि पवसे \\ इति द्वे हविष उत्तरे स्विष्टकृतः //
5.1.2.m: Among the sacrifices for the establishment of the fires (Agnyādheya), in that for [Agni] Pavamāna, "O Agni, you purify lifespans…" are the two subsequent [verses] for the oblation, [followed by those] for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.2.s: agne pāvaka rociṣā \\ ity uttarayoś catasra uttare sviṣṭakṛtaḥ /
5.1.2.d: अग्ने पावक रोचिषा \\ इत्य् उत्तरयोश् चतस्र उत्तरे स्विष्टकृतः /
5.1.2.m: "O purifying Agni, with radiant light…": the four subsequent [verses] for the two following [oblations], [followed by those] for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
For the one of four oblations, the ritual procedure is vairāja.
The two [verses] for the [oblation] to Agni and Viṣṇu are those handed down by tradition.

5.1.2.s: kim it te viṣṇa iti ṣaḍ uttareṣām /
5.1.2.d: किम् इत् ते विष्ण इति षड् उत्तरेषाम् /
5.1.2.m: "What, O Viṣṇu, is your…" are the six [verses] for the subsequent [three oblations].

5.1.2.s: punarādheye prayājānuyājānāṃ purastād vopariṣṭād vā vibhaktīḥ kuryāt \\ ye3 yajāmahe \ samidhaḥsamidho 'gnā ājyasya vyantu \\ agnir agnis \ tanūnapād agnā ājyasya vetu \\ agnimagnim \ iḍo 'gnā ājyasya vyantu \\ agneragner \ barhir agnā ājyasya vetu \\ agneragner iti / yathāmnāta uttamaḥ //
5.1.2.d: पुनराधेये प्रयाजानुयाजानां पुरस्ताद् वोपरिष्टाद् वा विभक्तीः कुर्यात् \\ ये3 यजामहे \ समिधःसमिधो ऽग्ना आज्यस्य व्यन्तु \\ अग्निर् अग्निस् \ तनूनपाद् अग्ना आज्यस्य वेतु \\ अग्निमग्निम् \ इडो ऽग्ना आज्यस्य व्यन्तु \\ अग्नेरग्नेर् \ बर्हिर् अग्ना आज्यस्य वेतु \\ अग्नेरग्नेर् इति / यथाम्नात उत्तमः //
5.1.2.m: At the re-establishment of the fires (Punarādheya), one may make case-inflections (vibhaktis) of [the word] Agni either before or after the fore-offerings and after-offerings: "We who sacrifice… May the kindling-sticks, the kindling-sticks, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter. Agni, Agni. May Tanūnapāt, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter. Agni, Agni. May the iḍā offerings, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter. Agni's, Agni's. May the sacrificial grass, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter. Agni's, Agni's." The last [fore-offering] is as handed down by tradition.

5.1.2.s: agnim̐ stomena bodhaya \\ iti ṣaḍ ājyabhāgahaviḥsviṣṭakṛtām /
5.1.2.d: अग्निम्̐ स्तोमेन बोधय \\ इति षड् आज्यभागहविःस्विष्टकृताम् /
5.1.2.m: "Awaken Agni with praise…" are the six [verses] for the clarified butter portions, the oblation, and the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.2.s: āgneyāvājyabhāgau \\ agnir mūrdhā \\ iti prajākāmasya paśukāmasya vā somasya loke kuryāt //
5.1.2.d: आग्नेयावाज्यभागौ \\ अग्निर् मूर्धा \\ इति प्रजाकामस्य पशुकामस्य वा सोमस्य लोके कुर्यात् //
5.1.2.m: The two clarified butter portions are addressed to Agni; in place of Soma, for one desiring offspring or one desiring cattle, he should recite: "Agni is the head…".

5.1.2.s: devaṃ barhir vasuvane vasudheyasya vetu \\ agneragner \ devo narāśam̐so vasuvane vasudheyasya vetu \\ agneragner iti / yathāmnāta uttamaḥ /
5.1.2.d: देवं बर्हिर् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु \\ अग्नेरग्नेर् \ देवो नराशम्̐सो वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु \\ अग्नेरग्नेर् इति / यथाम्नात उत्तमः /
5.1.2.m: "May the divine sacrificial grass, in the winning of wealth, partake of the treasure-store. Agni's, Agni's. May the divine Narāśaṃsa, in the winning of wealth, partake of the treasure-store. Agni's, Agni's." The last [after-offering] is as handed down by tradition.

5.1.2.s: agnaye jyotiṣmate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped vāruṇam̐ yavamayaṃ carum //
5.1.2.d: अग्नये ज्योतिष्मते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् वारुणम्̐ यवमयं चरुम् //
5.1.2.m: He should apportion [a cake] on eight potsherds to lustrous Agni, [and] a boiled oblation made of barley to Varuṇa.

5.1.2.s: tvam agne saprathā asi \ vṛṣā soma \\ iti vṛṣaṇvantāv ājyabhāgau //
5.1.2.d: त्वम् अग्ने सप्रथा असि \ वृषा सोम \\ इति वृषण्वन्ताव् आज्यभागौ //
5.1.2.m: "O Agni, you are widespread…", "Soma, the bull…" are the two clarified butter portions containing the word 'bull' (vṛṣaṇvant).

5.1.2.s: agnir jāto arocata \\ iti haviṣaś catasraḥ /
5.1.2.d: अग्निर् जातो अरोचत \\ इति हविषश् चतस्रः /
5.1.2.m: "Agni, being born, shone forth…" are the four [verses] of the oblation.

5.1.2.s: agnaye 'gnimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapen maitraṃ carum̐ sauryam ekakapālam agnaye vratapataye 'gnaye pathikṛte 'gnaye śucaye 'gnaye kṣāmavate 'gnaye tapasvate janadvate pāvakavate 'gnaye tantumate 'gnaye vivice 'ṣṭākapālān /
5.1.2.d: अग्नये ऽग्निमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेन् मैत्रं चरुम्̐ सौर्यम् एककपालम् अग्नये व्रतपतये ऽग्नये पथिकृते ऽग्नये शुचये ऽग्नये क्षामवते ऽग्नये तपस्वते जनद्वते पावकवते ऽग्नये तन्तुमते ऽग्नये विविचे ऽष्टाकपालान् /
5.1.2.m: He should apportion [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni possessed of fires, a boiled oblation to Mitra, [a cake] on one potsherd to Sūrya, [and cakes] on eight potsherds to Agni lord of vows, to Agni path-maker, to pure Agni, to scorched Agni, to ascetic Agni, to Agni with progeny, to Agni with purifiers, to Agni possessed of the thread, [and] to discriminating Agni.
"Agni is kindled by Agni…" are the sixteen [verses] of the oblations.

5.1.2.s: svayaṃ kṛṇvānas \ tvaṃ tantur iti tantumatyau /
5.1.2.d: स्वयं कृण्वानस् \ त्वं तन्तुर् इति तन्तुमत्यौ /
5.1.2.m: "Making by oneself…", "You are the thread…" are the two verses addressed to Agni possessed of the thread (tantumant).

5.1.2.s:
vi te viṣvag vātajūtāso agne \ bhāmāsaḥ śuce śucayaś caranti /
tuvimrakṣāso divyā navagvās \ vanā vananti dhṛṣatā rujantaḥ //
tvām agne mānuṣīr īḍate viśas\ hotrāvidam̐ vivicim̐ ratnadhātamam /
guhā santam̐ subhaga viśvadarśatam\ tuviṣvaṇasam̐ suyajaṃ ghṛtaśriyam //
iti vaivicyau /
5.1.2.d:
वि ते विष्वग् वातजूतासो अग्ने \ भामासः शुचे शुचयश् चरन्ति /
तुविम्रक्षासो दिव्या नवग्वास् \ वना वनन्ति धृषता रुजन्तः //
त्वाम् अग्ने मानुषीर् ईडते विशस्\ होत्राविदम्̐ विविचिम्̐ रत्नधातमम् /
गुहा सन्तम्̐ सुभग विश्वदर्शतम्\ तुविष्वणसम्̐ सुयजं घृतश्रियम् //
इति वैविच्यौ /

5.1.3.s: vaiśvadeve \\ agnaye mathyamānāyānubrūhi \\ ity ukte \\ abhi tvā deva savitar iti pratipadyate // dasyuhantamam iti viramati //
5.1.3.d: वैश्वदेवे \\ अग्नये मथ्यमानायानुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् उक्ते \\ अभि त्वा देव सवितर् इति प्रतिपद्यते // दस्युहन्तमम् इति विरमति //
5.1.3.m: At the Vaiśvadeva [seasonal offering], when it is said: "Recite for Agni being churned", he begins with: "Towards you, divine Savitṛ…"; he stops at: "…the greatest slayer of Dasyus".

5.1.3.s: agnaye jātāyānubrūhi \\ ity ukte dhanaṃjayam̐ raṇeraṇo3m iti pratipadyate // bibhrati \\ iti viramati //
5.1.3.d: अग्नये जातायानुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् उक्ते धनंजयम्̐ रणेरणो3म् इति प्रतिपद्यते // बिभ्रति \\ इति विरमति //
5.1.3.m: When it is said: "Recite for Agni who is born", he begins with: "Winner of booty, in battle after battle…"; he stops at: "…bearing".

5.1.3.s: agnaye prahriyamānāyānubrūhi \\ ity ukte viśām agnim̐ svadhvaro3m iti pratipadyate //
5.1.3.d: अग्नये प्रह्रियमानायानुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् उक्ते विशाम् अग्निम्̐ स्वध्वरो3म् इति प्रतिपद्यते //
5.1.3.m: When it is said: "Recite for Agni being carried forward", he begins with: "Agni of the clans, performing good sacrifices…".

5.1.3.s: yajñena yajñam iti paridadhāti /
5.1.3.d: यज्ञेन यज्ञम् इति परिदधाति /
5.1.3.m: He concludes with: "With sacrifice the sacrifice…".

5.1.3.s: atraiva tiṣṭhan sāmidhenīr anvāha //
5.1.3.d: अत्रैव तिष्ठन् सामिधेनीर् अन्वाह //
5.1.3.m: Standing right there, he recites the kindling verses (sāmidhenīs).

5.1.3.s: samidho agne \\ iti nava prayājāḥ //
5.1.3.d: समिधो अग्ने \\ इति नव प्रयाजाः //
5.1.3.m: "O Agni, the kindling-sticks…" are the nine fore-offerings.

5.1.3.s: agne yam \\ tvaṃ naḥ soma \\ iti viśvatavantāv ājyabhāgau //
5.1.3.d: अग्ने यम् \\ त्वं नः सोम \\ इति विश्वतवन्ताव् आज्यभागौ //
5.1.3.m: "O Agni, whom…", "O Soma, you to us…" are the two clarified butter portions containing the word 'all-around' (viśvatas).

5.1.3.s: agnir mūrdhā \ bhuvo yajñasya \\ iti ṣoḍaśa haviṣām //
5.1.3.d: अग्निर् मूर्धा \ भुवो यज्ञस्य \\ इति षोडश हविषाम् //
5.1.3.m: "Agni is the head…", "Become of the sacrifice…" are the sixteen [verses] of the oblations.

5.1.3.s: sa havyavāṭ \\ agnim̐ stomena \\ iti gāyatryau sam̐yājye //
5.1.3.d: स हव्यवाट् \\ अग्निम्̐ स्तोमेन \\ इति गायत्र्यौ सम्̐याज्ये //
5.1.3.m: "He, the conveyer of oblations…", "Awaken Agni with praise…" are the two gāyatrī concluding offering verses.

5.1.3.s: devaṃ barhir iti navānuyājāḥ //
5.1.3.d: देवं बर्हिर् इति नवानुयाजाः //
5.1.3.m: "Divine sacrificial grass…" are the nine after-offerings.

5.1.3.s: śaṃ nas \\ vājevāje \\ iti vājinasyāvyavānam̐ hotordhvajñur āsīno yajati / vājinasya \\ agne vīhi \\ ity anuvaṣaṭkaroti /
5.1.3.d: शं नस् \\ वाजेवाजे \\ इति वाजिनस्याव्यवानम्̐ होतोर्ध्वज्ञुर् आसीनो यजति / वाजिनस्य \\ अग्ने वीहि \\ इत्य् अनुवषट्करोति /
5.1.3.m: Without interruption, the hotṛ priest, seated with his right knee raised, makes the offering of the whey (vājina) with: "May [the horses] be auspicious to us…", "In every contest…"; he pronounces the secondary vaṣaṭ-call with: "Of the whey… O Agni, partake!".

5.1.3.s: varuṇapraghāseṣv agnipraṇayanakāle paścād āhavanīyasyopaviśati //
5.1.3.d: वरुणप्रघासेष्व् अग्निप्रणयनकाले पश्चाद् आहवनीयस्योपविशति //
5.1.3.m: In the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, at the time of carrying forward the fire, he sits behind the āhavanīya fire.

5.1.3.s: agnaye praṇīyamānāyānubrūhi \\ ity ukte pra devam iti pratipadyate / trir vacanasyārdharcam̐ śiṣṭvā viramati /
5.1.3.d: अग्नये प्रणीयमानायानुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् उक्ते प्र देवम् इति प्रतिपद्यते / त्रिर् वचनस्यार्धर्चम्̐ शिष्ट्वा विरमति /
5.1.3.m: When it is said: "Recite for Agni being carried forward", he begins with: "Forward to the god…"; having left over half a verse of the three-fold recitation, he pauses.

5.1.3.s: hute havyā no vakṣad ānuṣak \\ ity upottiṣṭhati \\ amṛtād iva janmanas \\ iti viramati /
5.1.3.d: हुते हव्या नो वक्षद् आनुषक् \\ इत्य् उपोत्तिष्ठति \\ अमृताद् इव जन्मनस् \\ इति विरमति /
5.1.3.m: When [the oblation] has been offered, he rises up with: "May he continuously convey our oblations…"; he stops at: "…as if from immortal birth".

5.1.3.s: tūṣṇīm anvety ādhānavelāyām \\ sahasaś cit sahīyān iti pratipadyate //
5.1.3.d: तूष्णीम् अन्वेत्य् आधानवेलायाम् \\ सहसश् चित् सहीयान् इति प्रतिपद्यते //
5.1.3.m: He follows silently; at the moment of setting down [the fire], he begins with: "Stronger even than the strong…".

5.1.3.s: tvaṃ dūtas \\ iti paridadhāti /
5.1.3.d: त्वं दूतस् \\ इति परिदधाति /
5.1.3.m: He concludes with: "You are the messenger…".

5.1.3.s: agnimanthanaprabhṛti vaiśvadevena vyākhyātam //
5.1.3.d: अग्निमन्थनप्रभृति वैश्वदेवेन व्याख्यातम् //
5.1.3.m: From the churning of fire onward, it is explained by the Vaiśvadeva [ritual].

5.1.3.s: agninā rayim aśnavat \\ gayasphānas \\ iti rayimantāv ājyabhāgau /
5.1.3.d: अग्निना रयिम् अश्नवत् \\ गयस्फानस् \\ इति रयिमन्ताव् आज्यभागौ /
5.1.3.m: "Through Agni one may attain wealth…", "Increaser of the home…" are the two clarified butter portions containing the word 'wealth' (rayimant).

5.1.3.s: ūrdhvaṃ pañca saṃcarebhyaḥ / caturṇām indrāgnī rocanā \\ ity aṣṭau //
5.1.3.d: ऊर्ध्वं पञ्च संचरेभ्यः / चतुर्णाम् इन्द्राग्नी रोचना \\ इत्य् अष्टौ //
5.1.3.m: After the five communal oblations, for the four [remaining ones], "Indra and Agni, lights…" are the eight [verses].

5.1.3.s: piprīhi devān \ agne yad adya \\ iti sviṣṭakṛtaḥ sam̐yājye /
5.1.3.d: पिप्रीहि देवान् \ अग्ने यद् अद्य \\ इति स्विष्टकृतः सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.3.m: "Please the gods…", "O Agni, what today…" are the two concluding offering verses of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.3.s: avabhṛthe 'ṣṭau dhvānena carati /
5.1.3.d: अवभृथे ऽष्टौ ध्वानेन चरति /
5.1.3.m: At the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), he performs eight [offerings] with a low murmuring tone.

5.1.3.s: prayājaprabhṛti yajati /
5.1.3.d: प्रयाजप्रभृति यजति /
5.1.3.m: He sacrifices starting from the fore-offerings.

5.1.3.s: barhiṣmantam udūhati //
5.1.3.d: बर्हिष्मन्तम् उदूहति //

5.1.3.s: svāhāgnīvaruṇau hotārau \\ iti sviṣṭakṛtsthāne //
5.1.3.d: स्वाहाग्नीवरुणौ होतारौ \\ इति स्विष्टकृत्स्थाने //
5.1.3.m: "Svāhā to Agni and Varuṇa, the two hotṛ priests…" in place of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.3.s: apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava \\ apsu me somas \\ ity apsumantāv ājyabhāgau //
5.1.3.d: अप्स्व् अग्ने सधिष् टव \\ अप्सु मे सोमस् \\ इत्य् अप्सुमन्ताव् आज्यभागौ //
5.1.3.m: "In the waters, O Agni, is your seat…", "In the waters, for me, Soma…" are the two clarified butter portions containing the word 'waters' (apsumant).

5.1.3.s: ud uttamam \ ava te heḍas \\ iti haviṣaḥ //
5.1.3.d: उद् उत्तमम् \ अव ते हेडस् \\ इति हविषः //
5.1.3.m: "Highest…", "Loosen your anger…" are the two [verses] of the oblation.

5.1.3.s: tvaṃ no agne \\ ity anūcya ye3 yajāmahe \\ agnīvaruṇau sviṣṭakṛtau \\ ayāṣṭām agnīvaruṇāv agneḥ priyā dhāmāni \\ ayāṣṭām̐ somasya priyā dhāmāni \\ ayāṣṭām̐ varuṇasya priyā dhāmāni \\ ayāṣṭāṃ devānām ājyapānāṃ priyā dhāmāni \ yakṣato 'gnīvaruṇayor hotroḥ priyā dhāmāni \ yakṣataḥ svau mahimānau \\ āyajeyātām ejyā iṣaḥ \ kṛṇutāṃ tāv adhvarā jātavedasau \ juṣetām̐ haviḥ \ sa tvaṃ nas \\ iti yajati /
5.1.3.d: त्वं नो अग्ने \\ इत्य् अनूच्य ये3 यजामहे \\ अग्नीवरुणौ स्विष्टकृतौ \\ अयाष्टाम् अग्नीवरुणाव् अग्नेः प्रिया धामानि \\ अयाष्टाम्̐ सोमस्य प्रिया धामानि \\ अयाष्टाम्̐ वरुणस्य प्रिया धामानि \\ अयाष्टां देवानाम् आज्यपानां प्रिया धामानि \ यक्षतो ऽग्नीवरुणयोर् होत्रोः प्रिया धामानि \ यक्षतः स्वौ महिमानौ \\ आयजेयाताम् एज्या इषः \ कृणुतां ताव् अध्वरा जातवेदसौ \ जुषेताम्̐ हविः \ स त्वं नस् \\ इति यजति /
5.1.3.m: Having recited: "You to us, O Agni…", he makes the offering saying: "We who sacrifice… Agni and Varuṇa, the two Sviṣṭakṛt deities. Agni and Varuṇa have sacrificed to Agni's dear dwellings; they have sacrificed to Soma's dear dwellings; they have sacrificed to Varuṇa's dear dwellings; they have sacrificed to the dear dwellings of the gods who drink clarified butter. May they two sacrifice to the dear dwellings of the hotṛ offices of Agni and Varuṇa; may they sacrifice to their own two greatnesses. May the two obtain by sacrifice refreshing foods to be obtained by sacrifice; may those two Jātavedases make the sacrificial rites; may they enjoy the oblation. So you to us…".

5.1.4.s: sākamedheṣu \\ agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanad iti ṣaḍ anīkavatasyaiṣa eva mṛte kalpaḥ /
5.1.4.d: साकमेधेषु \\ अग्निर् वृत्राणि जङ्घनद् इति षड् अनीकवतस्यैष एव मृते कल्पः /
5.1.4.m: In the Sākamedha rites, "Agni will slay the Vṛtras…" are the six [verses] for [Agni] Anīkavat; this very ritual procedure applies, except [for what is noted].
The two subsequent [verses] of the oblation are for [the Maruts] Sāṃtapana.

5.1.4.s: agniḥ pratnena manmanā \\ iti ṣaḍ gṛhamedhīyasya /
5.1.4.d: अग्निः प्रत्नेन मन्मना \\ इति षड् गृहमेधीयस्य /
5.1.4.m: "Agni by ancient thought…" are the six [verses] of the Gṛhamedhīya offering.
He sacrifices starting from the clarified butter portions.
Having recited a verse [as the invitatory verse], he performs the Sviṣṭakṛt offering with a verse [as the offering verse].
"I praise Agni…" are the six [verses] for [the Maruts] Krīḍin.
For [rites] ending with the Vaiśvakarmaṇa [offering], the ritual procedure is that relating to Vṛtra-slaying.
From the bringing forward of the fire onward, it is established as in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.

5.1.4.s: ūrdhvaṃ pañca saṃcarebhya // indrāgnī navatim iti ṣaṭ trayāṇām /
5.1.4.d: ऊर्ध्वं पञ्च संचरेभ्य // इन्द्राग्नी नवतिम् इति षट् त्रयाणाम् /
5.1.4.m: Above the five common [oblations], the six [verses] beginning with "Indra and Agni, ninety" belong to the three [oblations].

5.1.4.s: pitṛyajñe \\ uśantas tvā havāmahe \\ ity ekām̐ sāmidhenīṃ trir anvāha //
5.1.4.d: पितृयज्ञे \\ उशन्तस् त्वा हवामहे \\ इत्य् एकाम्̐ सामिधेनीं त्रिर् अन्वाह //
5.1.4.m: In the ancestral sacrifice, he recites the single kindling verse "Desiring thee, we summon" three times.

5.1.4.s: agne mahaṃ asi brāhmaṇa bhārata mānuṣa \\ iti na pravṛṇīte //
5.1.4.d: अग्ने महं असि ब्राह्मण भारत मानुष \\ इति न प्रवृणीते //
5.1.4.m: He does not choose [the hotṛ] with "Agni, thou art great, O brāhmaṇa, Bhārata, descendant of Manu."
He recites "Kindled by the gods, kindled by Manu" as handed down [in the sacred text].

5.1.4.s: agniṃ kavyavāhanam āvaha \\ iti sviṣṭakṛtpravāde kavyavāhanapravādaḥ /
5.1.4.d: अग्निं कव्यवाहनम् आवह \\ इति स्विष्टकृत्प्रवादे कव्यवाहनप्रवादः /
5.1.4.m: Instead of the mention of Sviṣṭakṛt, there is mention of Kavyavāhana: "Bring hither Agni Kavyavāhana."
He performs the fore-offerings and after-offerings without sacrificial grass.

5.1.4.s: ā no agne \ tvam̐ soma \\ iti jīvitavantāv ājyabhāgau /
5.1.4.d: आ नो अग्ने \ त्वम्̐ सोम \\ इति जीवितवन्ताव् आज्यभागौ /
5.1.4.m: The two clarified butter portions contain [the word] "life": "Come to us, O Agni" [and] "Thou, O Soma."
The next twelve [verses] belong to the oblations and the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings.
"This to the fathers" [and] "Let them arise" are transposed.
Of them, he makes one verse a half-verse portion.
He utters the vaṣaṭ-call with "Svadhā, homage!"
For the [offering to] the Ādityas, the ritual framework is that of the full-moon sacrifice.

5.1.4.s: sutrāmāṇam \\ mahīm ū ṣu \\ ity upām̐śuhaviṣaḥ /
5.1.4.d: सुत्रामाणम् \\ महीम् ऊ षु \\ इत्य् उपाम्̐शुहविषः /
5.1.4.m: "The good protector" [and] "Indeed, the great [mother]" belong to the oblation [offered] in a whisper.
The Śunāsīrīya is explained by the Vaiśvadeva.

5.1.4.s: ūrdhvaṃ pañca saṃcarebhyaḥ // pra vāyum iti ṣaṭ trayāṇām /
5.1.4.d: ऊर्ध्वं पञ्च संचरेभ्यः // प्र वायुम् इति षट् त्रयाणाम् /
5.1.4.m: Above the five common [oblations], the six [verses] beginning with "Forth to Vāyu" belong to the three [oblations].

5.1.4.s: upām̐śudevatānām upām̐śudevatām ādiśati yājyānuvākye ca \\ ajuṣata \\ avīvṛdhata \\ akṛta \\ iti copām̐śuvāyavyāḥ /
5.1.4.d: उपाम्̐शुदेवतानाम् उपाम्̐शुदेवताम् आदिशति याज्यानुवाक्ये च \\ अजुषत \\ अवीवृधत \\ अकृत \\ इति चोपाम्̐शुवायव्याः /
5.1.4.m: For the whisper deities, he designates the whisper deity and the two offering and invitatory verses; and "they enjoyed," "they increased," [and] "they made" belong to the whisper Vāyavya [offerings].

5.1.5.s: kāmyā upām̐śudevatāḥ / tāsv ekadhanam anādiṣṭadakṣiṇāsu dadyāt /
5.1.5.d: काम्या उपाम्̐शुदेवताः / तास्व् एकधनम् अनादिष्टदक्षिणासु दद्यात् /
5.1.5.m: The whisper deities belong to the desire-prompted rites. In those where no sacrificial gift is specified, he should give a single article of wealth.
In the battle rites, the ritual procedure is that relating to Vṛtra-slaying.
And in the sorcery rites, the ritual procedure is the expiation [procedure] of the "He who..." [rites].
For one desirous of a village, one desirous of prosperity, [and] one desirous of cattle, the two clarified butter portions contain [the word] "wealth".
For one desirous of a village and one desirous of prosperity, the two concluding offering verses contain [the word] "together"; for one desirous of cattle, they contain [the word] "thousand".

5.1.5.s: grāmakāmatantreṇaindrāgnena viyātsu viyāteṣu vā sajāteṣu yajeta /
5.1.5.d: ग्रामकामतन्त्रेणैन्द्राग्नेन वियात्सु वियातेषु वा सजातेषु यजेत /
5.1.5.m: With the ritual framework for one desirous of a village, one should sacrifice with the [offering] to Indra-and-Agni when kinsmen are about to depart or have departed.

5.1.5.s: tasyās \\ indrāgnī rocanā \\ iti dve haviṣaḥ /
5.1.5.d: तस्यास् \\ इन्द्राग्नी रोचना \\ इति द्वे हविषः /
5.1.5.m: For this rite, the two [verses] "Indra and Agni, the bright realms" belong to the oblation.
One who has a rival [sacrifices] according to the ritual procedure relating to Vṛtra-slaying.
The two clarified butter portions relate to Vṛtra-slaying.
The two [verses] "Indra and Agni, ninety" belong to the oblation.

5.1.5.s: juṣṭo damūnā \ agne śardha \\ iti śardhavatyau sam̐yājye /
5.1.5.d: जुष्टो दमूना \ अग्ने शर्ध \\ इति शर्धवत्यौ सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.5.m: "Enjoyed, the dweller in the house" [and] "O Agni, strength" are the two concluding offering verses containing [the word] "strength".
For one desirous of offspring, the two clarified butter portions contain [the word] "bull".

5.1.5.s: pra vām arcanti \\ iti dve haviṣa / uttare sviṣṭakṛtaḥ /
5.1.5.d: प्र वाम् अर्चन्ति \\ इति द्वे हविष / उत्तरे स्विष्टकृतः /
5.1.5.m: The two [verses] "They sing to you two" belong to the oblation; the two subsequent ones belong to the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.5.s: saṃgrāmam abhiprayān saṃgrāmasam̐yājye / sam̐yatyaitābhyām iṣṭvā vāniṣṭvā vā / jitvottarayā yajeta /
5.1.5.d: संग्रामम् अभिप्रयान् संग्रामसम्̐याज्ये / सम्̐यत्यैताभ्याम् इष्ट्वा वानिष्ट्वा वा / जित्वोत्तरया यजेत /
5.1.5.m: When advancing toward battle, [he employs] the two concluding offering verses for battle; having joined [in battle], whether he has sacrificed with these two or not, having conquered he should sacrifice with the subsequent one.

5.1.5.s: tasyās \\ indrāgnī rocanā \\ iti dve haviṣa / uttare pūrvayoḥ /
5.1.5.d: तस्यास् \\ इन्द्राग्नी रोचना \\ इति द्वे हविष / उत्तरे पूर्वयोः /
5.1.5.m: For this [sacrifice], the two [verses] "Indra and Agni, the bright realms" belong to the oblation; the two subsequent ones are [the concluding verses] of the earlier two.

5.1.5.s: paraṃ janapadam abhiprayān dvihaviṣā yajeta / yadi senayā vārtraghnaḥ kalpa / yadi janena grāmakāmaṃ tantram //
5.1.5.d: परं जनपदम् अभिप्रयान् द्विहविषा यजेत / यदि सेनया वार्त्रघ्नः कल्प / यदि जनेन ग्रामकामं तन्त्रम् //
5.1.5.m: When setting out toward another country, he should sacrifice with a two-oblation [rite]; if with an army, the ritual procedure relates to Vṛtra-slaying; if with common people, the ritual framework is for one desirous of a village.

5.1.5.s: yā vām̐ santi \\ iti dvihaviṣoś catasraḥ /
5.1.5.d: या वाम्̐ सन्ति \\ इति द्विहविषोश् चतस्रः /
5.1.5.m: The four [verses] beginning with "Those which are yours" belong to the two oblations.
When settling on a field, he should sacrifice with a three-oblation [rite].
For this [sacrifice], the ritual framework is for one desirous of a village.
The six [verses] beginning with "Those which are yours" belong to the oblations.

5.1.5.s: sam̐sam it \ sakhāyas \\ iti sam̐vatyau sam̐yājye /
5.1.5.d: सम्̐सम् इत् \ सखायस् \\ इति सम्̐वत्यौ सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.5.m: "Together indeed" [and] "Friends" are the two concluding offering verses containing [the word] "together".

5.1.5.s: agnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet kāmāya sarvakāmāya /
5.1.5.d: अग्नये वैश्वानराय द्वादशकपालं निर्वपेत् कामाय सर्वकामाय /
5.1.5.m: He should apportion a twelve-potsherd [cake] to Agni Vaiśvānara for a desire, for all desires.

5.1.5.s: vaiśvānaro na ūtyā \ pṛṣṭo divi \\ iti haviṣo / 'nāmnātayājyānuvākyānām ete vaiśvānarīyāṇām //
5.1.5.d: वैश्वानरो न ऊत्या \ पृष्टो दिवि \\ इति हविषो / ऽनाम्नातयाज्यानुवाक्यानाम् एते वैश्वानरीयाणाम् //
5.1.5.m: "Vaiśvānara, for our protection" [and] "Touching the sky" belong to the oblation; these belong to the Vaiśvānara [oblations] whose offering and invitatory verses are not explicitly handed down.

5.1.5.s: agnir mūrdhā \ bhuvo yajñasya \\ ity āgneyānām //
5.1.5.d: अग्निर् मूर्धा \ भुवो यज्ञस्य \\ इत्य् आग्नेयानाम् //
5.1.5.m: "Agni is the head" [and] "Be of the sacrifice" belong to the offerings to Agni.

5.1.5.s: agnīṣomā savedasā \ yuvam etāni \\ ity agnīṣomīyāṇām /
5.1.5.d: अग्नीषोमा सवेदसा \ युवम् एतानि \\ इत्य् अग्नीषोमीयाणाम् /
5.1.5.m: "Agni and Soma, possessing possessions" [and] "You two, these" belong to the offerings to Agni-and-Soma.
If he intends to violate an agreement before the appointed time, he should sacrifice.
If he intends to rise up for the acquisition of gain, he should sacrifice.
The two clarified butter portions contain [the word] "wealth".
The two [verses] beginning with "The righteous one" belong to the oblation.

5.1.5.s: iḍām agne \ tvaṃ no agne \\ iti sanimatyau sam̐yājye /
5.1.5.d: इडाम् अग्ने \ त्वं नो अग्ने \\ इति सनिमत्यौ सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.5.m: "Refreshment, O Agni" [and] "Thou to us, O Agni" are the two concluding offering verses containing [the word] "gain".
When he has acquired [the gain], then he should sacrifice with the subsequent one.

5.1.5.s: yaṃ dviṣyāt tasmai sanim̐ sātāṃ gāṃ kaṇṭhabandham ekahāyanaṃ dadyāt //
5.1.5.d: यं द्विष्यात् तस्मै सनिम्̐ सातां गां कण्ठबन्धम् एकहायनं दद्यात् //
5.1.5.m: To him whom he hates, he should give as a sacrificial gift a cow obtained [as gain], bound by the neck, one year old.
The two [verses] beginning with "Of Vaiśvānara" belong to the oblation.
If he is about to eat food that is spoiled or unfit to be eaten, he should sacrifice.
The sacrificial gift is lead or a black garment.
The two clarified butter portions contain [the word] "protector".

5.1.5.s: viśvam̐ vivyāca \\ iti dve haviṣa / uttare sviṣṭakṛtaḥ /
5.1.5.d: विश्वम्̐ विव्याच \\ इति द्वे हविष / उत्तरे स्विष्टकृतः /
5.1.5.m: "He encompassed all"—these two are for the oblation; the subsequent two are for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
Having sacrificed with this, or without having sacrificed, having consumed [the food], one should sacrifice with the subsequent one.
And the offering and invitatory verses are explained.

5.1.5.s: tathā sāṃgrāmikyau ya iched ayam eva rājā syād yāvad imān yavān vrīhīn vādadhīyet /
5.1.5.d: तथा सांग्रामिक्यौ य इछेद् अयम् एव राजा स्याद् यावद् इमान् यवान् व्रीहीन् वादधीयेत् /
5.1.5.m: Similarly the two battle rites: he who desires, 'May this one alone be king, as long as he should store these barleys or rices.'

5.1.5.s: tasya ced aparo dhāveta vārtraghnaḥ kalpaḥ / yadi mṛtyor jīvitavān /
5.1.5.d: तस्य चेद् अपरो धावेत वार्त्रघ्नः कल्पः / यदि मृत्योर् जीवितवान् /
5.1.5.m: If another should attack him, the ritual procedure is the Vṛtra-slaying one; if he has survived death, [the same].
The two clarified butter portions contain [words denoting] 'life'.
The two concluding offering verses contain [the word] 'pārayat'.
A two-oblation rite is for one desiring prosperity.
This boiled oblation is the measure of a span.

5.1.5.s: sarvasvaṃ dattvāgnaye jātavedasa iti trihaviṣā yajeta /
5.1.5.d: सर्वस्वं दत्त्वाग्नये जातवेदस इति त्रिहविषा यजेत /
5.1.5.m: Having given away all his possessions, one should sacrifice with a three-oblation rite to Agni Jātavedas.
Its ritual framework is that for one desiring cattle.

5.1.5.s: ny agniṃ jātavedasam iti dvihaviṣoś catasraḥ /
5.1.5.d: न्य् अग्निं जातवेदसम् इति द्विहविषोश् चतस्रः /
5.1.5.m: "Down [bring] Agni Jātavedas": [these are] the four [verses] for the two oblations.
[The verses] for the Vaiśvānara [oblation] have been handed down by tradition.

5.1.5.s: upavatsv aśanaṃ bhuktvā sam̐srave grāmasya purastād vāgyato vasati /
5.1.5.d: उपवत्स्व् अशनं भुक्त्वा सम्̐स्रवे ग्रामस्य पुरस्ताद् वाग्यतो वसति /
5.1.5.m: Having eaten fasting food during the fasting days, he stays, restrained in speech, in the confluent waters [or water gathering] in front of the village.

5.1.5.s: śvobhūte 'gnim̐ samāropya mathitvā yajñāyudhair anvetyāgnaye surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet /
5.1.5.d: श्वोभूते ऽग्निम्̐ समारोप्य मथित्वा यज्ञायुधैर् अन्वेत्याग्नये सुरभिमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत् /
5.1.5.m: On the next day, having mounted the fire [into the kindling sticks], having churned it out, and having accompanied it with the sacrificial utensils, he should apportion an eight-potsherd [cake] to fragrant Agni.
The two clarified butter portions contain [words denoting] 'guarding'.
Two [verses] are for the oblation; the subsequent two are for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.5.s: agnaye pavamānāyeti trihaviṣā gṛhān etya yajeta /
5.1.5.d: अग्नये पवमानायेति त्रिहविषा गृहान् एत्य यजेत /
5.1.5.m: Having come to the house, he should sacrifice with a three-oblation rite to Agni Pavamāna.
"An eight-potsherd cake to Agni": [he sacrifices] with a three-oblation rite.

5.1.5.s: yaḥ parajanapadāt senayābhinirjitya harati sa nṛjyāyaṃ jitvottarayā yajeta /
5.1.5.d: यः परजनपदात् सेनयाभिनिर्जित्य हरति स नृज्यायं जित्वोत्तरया यजेत /
5.1.5.m: He who, having conquered [the enemy] from a foreign territory by means of an army, carries off [booty], having won superiority over men, should sacrifice with the subsequent [offering].

5.1.5.s: tasyāṃ mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca nas \\ ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām iti dyāvāpṛthivīyasya /
5.1.5.d: तस्यां मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नस् \\ घृतवती भुवनानाम् इति द्यावापृथिवीयस्य /
5.1.5.m: In it: "Great Heaven and Earth for us", "Possessing clarified butter, of the creatures" are for that to Heaven and Earth.

5.1.5.s: agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped brāhmaṇaḥ kāmāya sarvakāmāya /
5.1.5.d: अग्नीषोमीयम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् ब्राह्मणः कामाय सर्वकामाय /
5.1.5.m: A brahmin desiring any wish should apportion an eleven-potsherd [cake] to Agni-Soma.

5.1.5.s: agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapec chyāmākam̐ vasantā brahmavarcasakāmaḥ /
5.1.5.d: अग्नीषोमीयम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेच् छ्यामाकम्̐ वसन्ता ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः /
5.1.5.m: One desiring spiritual luster should apportion an eleven-potsherd [cake] of wild millet to Agni-Soma in spring.

5.1.5.s: pṛthupājāstam̐ sabādhas \\ iti ṣaḍ dhāyyāḥ / ṣaḍ uttarā ājyabhāgahaviḥsviṣṭakṛtām /
5.1.5.d: पृथुपाजास्तम्̐ सबाधस् \\ इति षड् धाय्याः / षड् उत्तरा आज्यभागहविःस्विष्टकृताम् /
5.1.5.m: "Of broad splendor", "With distress": [these are] the six insertion verses; the six subsequent ones are for the clarified butter portions, the oblation, and the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
One desiring cattle should apportion a boiled oblation of half-ground [grains] to Soma-Pūṣan.
"O Soma and Pūṣan": these two are for the oblation.

5.1.5.s: uta no brahman \ nū no rāsva \\ iti sahasravatyau sam̐yājye /
5.1.5.d: उत नो ब्रह्मन् \ नू नो रास्व \\ इति सहस्रवत्यौ सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.5.m: "And to us, O Brahman", "Now give to us": these two concluding offering verses contain [the word] 'thousand'.
One desiring the office of domestic priest should apportion a boiled oblation to Soma-Indra.
Its ritual framework is that for one desiring a village.

5.1.5.s: tvā yujā tava tat soma \\ iti dve haviṣaḥ /
5.1.5.d: त्वा युजा तव तत् सोम \\ इति द्वे हविषः /
5.1.5.m: "With you as ally", "That of yours, O Soma": these two are for the oblation.

5.1.5.s: āgnivāruṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapet samāntam abhidruhyāmayāvī vā /
5.1.5.d: आग्निवारुणं चरुं निर्वपेत् समान्तम् अभिद्रुह्यामयावी वा /
5.1.5.m: One who is chronically ill or having plotted against an enemy for a full year should apportion a boiled oblation to Agni-Varuṇa.

5.1.5.s: tvaṃ no agne \ sa tvaṃ no agne \\ iti haviṣaḥ /
5.1.5.d: त्वं नो अग्ने \ स त्वं नो अग्ने \\ इति हविषः /
5.1.5.m: "You to us, O Agni", "So you to us, O Agni": these are for the oblation.

5.1.6.s: saumāraudraṃ ghṛte caruṃ nirvapec chuklānām̐ vrīhīṇāṃ prādeśamātraṃ brahmavarcasakāmaḥ /
5.1.6.d: सौमारौद्रं घृते चरुं निर्वपेच् छुक्लानाम्̐ व्रीहीणां प्रादेशमात्रं ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः /
5.1.6.m: One desiring spiritual luster should apportion a boiled oblation of white rice in clarified butter, the measure of a span, to Soma-Rudra.
One should sacrifice on the full-moon day in the month of Taiṣa.

5.1.6.s: nāsya tām̐ rātrīm apo gṛhān prahareyuḥ /
5.1.6.d: नास्य ताम्̐ रात्रीम् अपो गृहान् प्रहरेयुः /
5.1.6.m: They should not carry water to his house during that night.
They perform the functions of water with clarified butter, in the sacrifice and in the Agnihotra.
Having enclosed [the space], he proceeds when the [sun's] rays are rising.

5.1.6.s: agnim̐ vaḥ pūrvyaṃ girā \ makṣū devavatas \\ iti manor ṛcaḥ ṣaḍdhāyyāḥ /
5.1.6.d: अग्निम्̐ वः पूर्व्यं गिरा \ मक्षू देववतस् \\ इति मनोर् ऋचः षड्धाय्याः /
5.1.6.m: "Agni to you, the first, with song", "Quickly, of him who has gods": these verses of Manu are the six insertion verses.
The two clarified butter portions are Vṛtra-slaying.
"O Soma and Rudra, you two": these two are for the oblation.
One should sacrifice on the same day with the offering to Soma-Pūṣan at the end of the full-moon sacrifice.

5.1.6.s: saumāraudraṃ caruṃ nirvapet kṛṣṇānām̐ vrīhīṇām abhicaran /
5.1.6.d: सौमारौद्रं चरुं निर्वपेत् कृष्णानाम्̐ व्रीहीणाम् अभिचरन् /
5.1.6.m: Practicing sorcery, one should apportion a boiled oblation of black rice to Soma-Rudra.
The sacrificial grass is made of reed; the sacrificial fuel is of Vibhīdaka wood.
The two [verses] beginning 'O Soma and Rudra, tear away' are for the oblation.

5.1.6.s: saumāraudraṃ caruṃ nirvapet kṛṣṇaśuklānām̐ vrīhīṇām̐ yaḥ kāmayeta dvitīyo 'sya sapatno viṣaye syād iti /
5.1.6.d: सौमारौद्रं चरुं निर्वपेत् कृष्णशुक्लानाम्̐ व्रीहीणाम्̐ यः कामयेत द्वितीयो ऽस्य सपत्नो विषये स्याद् इति /
5.1.6.m: One should apportion a boiled oblation to Soma and Rudra of black and white rice for one who desires, 'May a second rival of his be in the realm.'

5.1.6.s: ardham̐ śaramayaṃ barhir bhavaty ardho vaibhīdaka idhmaḥ /
5.1.6.d: अर्धम्̐ शरमयं बर्हिर् भवत्य् अर्धो वैभीदक इध्मः /
5.1.6.m: Half of the sacrificial grass is made of reed; half of the sacrificial fuel is of bibhītaka wood.
He cooks [it] when milk is poured over it.
One should apportion a curd oblation to Soma and Rudra.

5.1.6.s: sāmidhenīr anuvakṣyan hotā svapāṭhaḥ saṃmukhaṃ pariṇahyate / samāpte 'raṇyaṃ parāṇīya vidarśayet /
5.1.6.d: सामिधेनीर् अनुवक्ष्यन् होता स्वपाठः संमुखं परिणह्यते / समाप्ते ऽरण्यं पराणीय विदर्शयेत् /
5.1.6.m: About to recite the kindling verses, the hotṛ priest, knowing his recitation well, ties himself up in front; when it is finished, having led him away into the forest, he should cause him to see [it].

5.1.6.s: tasmā anaḍvāhaṃ dadyāt taṃ ghnīta tasyāśnīyād anneṣṭidakṣiṇā /
5.1.6.d: तस्मा अनड्वाहं दद्यात् तं घ्नीत तस्याश्नीयाद् अन्नेष्टिदक्षिणा /
5.1.6.m: To him he should give an ox; he may slaughter it; he should eat of it; [this is] the sacrificial gift of the food-offering.

5.1.6.s: āgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped abhicarann abhicaryamāṇo vā /
5.1.6.d: आग्नावैष्णवम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेद् अभिचरन्न् अभिचर्यमाणो वा /
5.1.6.m: One should apportion a sacrificial cake on eleven potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu, practicing sorcery or when being targeted by sorcery.
He should also sacrifice with clarified butter to Sarasvatī.
For one targeted by sorcery, the ritual procedure is the expiation; for one practicing sorcery, [it is] the vārtraghna.

5.1.6.s: agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā \\ agnāviṣṇū mahi dhāma priyam̐ vām ity āgnāvaiṣṇavasya // pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī \ sarasvaty abhi no neṣi vasyas \\ iti sārasvatasya /
5.1.6.d: अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसा \\ अग्नाविष्णू महि धाम प्रियम्̐ वाम् इत्य् आग्नावैष्णवस्य // पावका नः सरस्वती \ सरस्वत्य् अभि नो नेषि वस्यस् \\ इति सारस्वतस्य /
5.1.6.m: 'O Agni and Viṣṇu, in harmony', 'O Agni and Viṣṇu, your great dear abode'—these are for the [oblation] to Agni and Viṣṇu; 'Purifying us, Sarasvatī', 'O Sarasvatī, lead us to greater fortune'—these are for the [oblation] to Sarasvatī.
For one desiring sight, the two clarified butter portions contain the word viśva.
[The rules for] one who should apportion [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu when targeted by sorcery have been explained.

5.1.6.s: tathā sāṃgrāmikīm̐ yadi manyeta prati purastāc carantīti \\ agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā \\ iti tisraḥ / tāsāṃ dve puronuvākye kuryād ekām̐ yājyāṃ tathā sārasvatasya /
5.1.6.d: तथा सांग्रामिकीम्̐ यदि मन्येत प्रति पुरस्ताच् चरन्तीति \\ अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसा \\ इति तिस्रः / तासां द्वे पुरोनुवाक्ये कुर्याद् एकाम्̐ याज्यां तथा सारस्वतस्य /
5.1.6.m: Likewise [the rite] concerning battle; if he should think: 'They are approaching from the front', [there are] three verses beginning 'O Agni and Viṣṇu, in harmony'; of them he should make two invitatory verses and one offering verse; likewise for the [oblation] to Sarasvatī.

5.1.6.s: āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ prātaraṣṭākapālam ity adhvarakalpāhnaḥ kāleṣu / pṛthaktantrānūbandhyākāle maitrāvaruṇa ekakapālaḥ payasyā vā /
5.1.6.d: आग्नावैष्णवं प्रातरष्टाकपालम् इत्य् अध्वरकल्पाह्नः कालेषु / पृथक्तन्त्रानूबन्ध्याकाले मैत्रावरुण एककपालः पयस्या वा /
5.1.6.m: The [cake] on eight potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu in the morning, [this is] during the times of the adhvarakalpa day; [there is] a separate ritual framework: at the time of the anūbandhyā cow, [a cake] on one potsherd to Mitra and Varuṇa, or a curd offering.

5.1.6.s: yasya bhrātṛvyaḥ somena yajeta sutyādhvarakalpam̐ saṃdadhyāt /
5.1.6.d: यस्य भ्रातृव्यः सोमेन यजेत सुत्याध्वरकल्पम्̐ संदध्यात् /
5.1.6.m: He whose rival sacrifices with Soma should connect the soma-pressing day with the adhvarakalpa.
The two [verses] for the [oblation] to Agni and Viṣṇu are traditionally handed down; likewise for the [oblation] to Sarasvatī.

5.1.6.s: bṛhaspate juṣasva nas \\ evā pitre \\ iti bārhaspatyasyottare maitrāvaruṇasya /
5.1.6.d: बृहस्पते जुषस्व नस् \\ एवा पित्रे \\ इति बार्हस्पत्यस्योत्तरे मैत्रावरुणस्य /
5.1.6.m: 'O Bṛhaspati, take pleasure in us', 'Thus to the Father'—these are for the [oblation] to Bṛhaspati; the next two are for the [oblation] to Mitra and Varuṇa.
On the eighth, four [verses] are explained by recitation.

5.1.6.s: vṛṣṭikāmasya \\ aurvabhṛguvad \ āsavam iti dhāyye / ṣaḍ uttarā ājyabhāgahaviḥsviṣṭakṛtām /
5.1.6.d: वृष्टिकामस्य \\ और्वभृगुवद् \ आसवम् इति धाय्ये / षड् उत्तरा आज्यभागहविःस्विष्टकृताम् /
5.1.6.m: For one desiring rain, 'Like Aurva and Bhṛgu', 'The pressing' are the two inserting verses; the next six are for the clarified butter portions, the oblation, and the Sviṣṭakṛt.

5.1.6.s: mārutam adhiśritya prāk paryagnikaraṇāt priyaṅgave gomūtrasyāścotayet //
5.1.6.d: मारुतम् अधिश्रित्य प्राक् पर्यग्निकरणात् प्रियङ्गवे गोमूत्रस्याश्चोतयेत् //
5.1.6.m: Having placed the [caru] to the Maruts on the fire, before carrying fire around it, he should sprinkle cow's urine on the panic-seed.

5.1.6.s: priyā vo nāma \ śriyase \\ iti dve haviṣaḥ /
5.1.6.d: प्रिया वो नाम \ श्रियसे \\ इति द्वे हविषः /
5.1.6.m: 'Dear are your names', 'For glory' are the two [verses] for the oblation.

5.1.6.s: trayodaśakapāle yadi gauḥ sā dakṣiṇā / yathākāmaṃ putrayoḥ /
5.1.6.d: त्रयोदशकपाले यदि गौः सा दक्षिणा / यथाकामं पुत्रयोः /
5.1.6.m: In the case of the [cake] on thirteen potsherds, if there is a cow, that is the sacrificial gift; according to desire in the case of the two sons.

5.1.6.s: maruto yad dha vo divaḥ \ praiṣām ajmeṣu \\ iti haviṣaḥ /
5.1.6.d: मरुतो यद् ध वो दिवः \ प्रैषाम् अज्मेषु \\ इति हविषः /
5.1.6.m: 'O Maruts, whatever from heaven', 'In their courses forth' are for the oblation.
In the case of the [cake] on seven potsherds, there are eleven kindling verses of the Kayāśubhīya hymn; three times the first and the last.
'Agni drives away the demons'—[with this verse and its companion are] the two clarified butter portions.
The remaining four are for the oblation and the Sviṣṭakṛt.

5.1.7.s: aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapen mārutam̐ saptakapālam̐ rājanyaṃ bhūtikāmam̐ yājayet //
5.1.7.d: ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेन् मारुतम्̐ सप्तकपालम्̐ राजन्यं भूतिकामम्̐ याजयेत् //
5.1.7.m: One should apportion [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra and [a cake] on seven potsherds to the Maruts; he should sacrifice for a noble who desires prosperity.

5.1.7.s: indram̐ vo viśvatas pari \\ ā te śuṣmas \\ ity aindrasyottare mārutasya /
5.1.7.d: इन्द्रम्̐ वो विश्वतस् परि \\ आ ते शुष्मस् \\ इत्य् ऐन्द्रस्योत्तरे मारुतस्य /
5.1.7.m: 'Indra from all sides for you', 'Unto you your strength'—these are for the [oblation] to Indra; the next two are for that to the Maruts.

5.1.7.s: aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapen mārutam̐ saptakapālam̐ yaḥ kāmayeta viṭ ca kṣatraṃ ca samāsādyeyātām iti /
5.1.7.d: ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेन् मारुतम्̐ सप्तकपालम्̐ यः कामयेत विट् च क्षत्रं च समासाद्येयाताम् इति /
5.1.7.m: One should apportion [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra and [a cake] on seven potsherds to the Maruts for one who desires, 'May the people and the nobility come into agreement.'

5.1.7.s: yadi kāmayetāturmuhyam̐ syād iti haviṣī āsādya pūrvārdhe 'nyāṃ grāmasya gām apākuryāt paścārdhe 'nyām api / te saṃgachete /
5.1.7.d: यदि कामयेतातुर्मुह्यम्̐ स्याद् इति हविषी आसाद्य पूर्वार्धे ऽन्यां ग्रामस्य गाम् अपाकुर्यात् पश्चार्धे ऽन्याम् अपि / ते संगछेते /
5.1.7.m: If he desires: 'May there be mutual infatuation', having set down the two oblations, he should drive away one cow to the eastern part of the village and another also to the western part; let them meet together.
Having cut off a portion of the [cake] to Indra, he causes [the hotṛ] to recite: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for Indra.'

5.1.7.s: ā tū na indra \\ ity anvāha /
5.1.7.d: आ तू न इन्द्र \\ इत्य् अन्वाह /

5.1.7.m: Having caused to call out, he issues the call: 'Sacrifice to the Maruts.'
He sacrifices with: 'Your spears, O Maruts.'
Having cut off a portion of the [cake] to the Maruts, he causes [the hotṛ] to recite: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for the Maruts.'

5.1.7.s: maruto yad dha vo balam ity anvāha /
5.1.7.d: मरुतो यद् ध वो बलम् इत्य् अन्वाह /
5.1.7.m: He recites: 'O Maruts, whatever is your strength.'
Having caused to call out, he issues the call: 'Sacrifice to Indra.'
He sacrifices with: 'You, O great Indra.'

5.1.7.s: purutrā hi sadṛṅṅ asi \\ iti sam̐yājye /
5.1.7.d: पुरुत्रा हि सदृङ्ङ् असि \\ इति सम्̐याज्ये /
5.1.7.m: 'For in many places you are uniform'—these two are the concluding offering verses.
In the Sviṣṭakṛt and in the sūktavāka recitation, it is indicated according to what is sacrificed.

5.1.7.s: yadi kāmayeta kalpetety ete eva haviṣī nirupya yathāyatham̐ yajet / kalpate 'ha /
5.1.7.d: यदि कामयेत कल्पेतेत्य् एते एव हविषी निरुप्य यथायथम्̐ यजेत् / कल्पते ऽह /
5.1.7.m: If he desires: 'May it succeed', having apportioned these same two oblations, he should sacrifice according to the proper order; indeed, it succeeds.

5.1.7.s: aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapen mārutam̐ saptakapālam abhicaran /
5.1.7.d: ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेन् मारुतम्̐ सप्तकपालम् अभिचरन् /
5.1.7.m: One should apportion [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra and [a cake] on seven potsherds to the Maruts, practicing sorcery.
He should cut off a portion from the top of the [cake] to Indra without turning it over, and from the bottom of the [cake] to the Maruts.

5.1.7.s: aindram ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapen mārutīm āmikṣām̐ rājanyaṃ grāmakāmam̐ yājayet /
5.1.7.d: ऐन्द्रम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेन् मारुतीम् आमिक्षाम्̐ राजन्यं ग्रामकामम्̐ याजयेत् /
5.1.7.m: One should apportion [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra and a curd oblation to the Maruts; he should sacrifice for a noble who desires a village.

5.1.7.s: pātryām̐ vyuduhyāmikṣāmadhye puroḍāśaṃ nidhāya samavadāya pracarati //
5.1.7.d: पात्र्याम्̐ व्युदुह्यामिक्षामध्ये पुरोडाशं निधाय समवदाय प्रचरति //
5.1.7.m: Having pushed aside [the curd] in the vessel and placed the sacrificial cake in the middle of the curd oblation, he cuts off together and proceeds.
He causes [the hotṛ] to recite: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for Indra and the Maruts.'
Having caused to call out, he issues the call: 'Sacrifice to Indra and the Maruts.'
The offering verse and invitatory verse are addressed to Indra and the Maruts.
One should apportion [a cake] on twenty-one potsherds to the Maruts, practicing sorcery.

5.1.7.s: ājyabhāgābhyāṃ pracarya barhiṣi puroḍāśaṃ nidhāya sphyena \\ idam aham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya \\ iti sphyena prāñcam̐ saṃbhinatti //
5.1.7.d: आज्यभागाभ्यां प्रचर्य बर्हिषि पुरोडाशं निधाय स्फ्येन \\ इदम् अहम् अमुष्यामुष्यायणस्य \\ इति स्फ्येन प्राञ्चम्̐ संभिनत्ति //
5.1.7.m: Having proceeded with the two clarified butter portions, having placed the sacrificial cake on the sacrificial grass, he cleaves it forwards with the wooden sword, saying: 'Here I, of such and such lineage, [cleave] such and such.'
He praises the wooden sword with: 'With this, a tiger.'

5.1.7.s: kālātipattau pāthikṛtī paśau darśapūrṇamāsayoś cāturmāsyaparvasu navāśane vāgrāyaṇasya /
5.1.7.d: कालातिपत्तौ पाथिकृती पशौ दर्शपूर्णमासयोश् चातुर्मास्यपर्वसु नवाशने वाग्रायणस्य /
5.1.7.m: In the case of a lapse of time, the [two cakes] for Pathikṛt [are offered] in the animal sacrifice, in the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, in the seasonal sacrifices, or at the first-fruits sacrifice in the eating of new grain.
For those desiring chieftainship of a troop or those who are disobedient, the offering is to the lord of troops.
The ritual procedure for the four [oblations] is the expiatory one; for the three, it is the Vṛtra-slaying one.
"O Agni, lead": [these] sixteen are for the oblations.
He should sacrifice also to Viṣṇu with clarified butter.

5.1.7.s: agnaye rudravate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yaḥ kāmayetarudrāyāsya paśūn apidadhyād iti /
5.1.7.d: अग्नये रुद्रवते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यः कामयेतरुद्रायास्य पशून् अपिदध्याद् इति /
5.1.7.m: He should apportion [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni accompanied by Rudra, if he wishes: 'May he shut up his cattle for Rudra.'

5.1.7.s: yadi kāmayeta śāmyed ity agnaye surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapet /
5.1.7.d: यदि कामयेत शाम्येद् इत्य् अग्नये सुरभिमते ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत् /
5.1.7.m: If he wishes: 'May it be appeased,' he should apportion [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni possessing fragrance.
The [mantras] for the clarified butter portions, the oblations, and the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings have been explained.

5.1.7.d: अग्नये ऽन्नवते ऽन्नादायान्नपतये ऽष्टाकपालम् अष्टाकपालान् वा /
5.1.7.m: [He should apportion a cake] on eight potsherds, or [three cakes each] on eight potsherds, to Agni possessing food, eating food, [and] the lord of food.
"For him whose food is oxen" [and] "Blown upon by the wind" are the two [verses] for the oblation.

5.1.7.s: agnaye rakṣoghne 'ṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yo rakṣobhyo bibhīyāt /
5.1.7.d: अग्नये रक्षोघ्ने ऽष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यो रक्षोभ्यो बिभीयात् /
5.1.7.m: He should apportion [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni the slayer of Rakṣases, if he fears Rakṣases.

5.1.7.s: kṛṇuṣva pājas \\ ity ekādaśa sāmidhenīḥ / triḥ prathamottame //
5.1.7.d: कृणुष्व पाजस् \\ इत्य् एकादश सामिधेनीः / त्रिः प्रथमोत्तमे //
5.1.7.m: With "Display your strength" [there are] eleven kindling verses; three times the first and the last.
"Agni drives away the Rakṣases" are the two clarified butter portions.
The remaining four are for the oblation and the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.7.s: āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirvaped yo rāṣṭre spardhetānnādyakāmo vā /
5.1.7.d: आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निर्वपेद् यो राष्ट्रे स्पर्धेतान्नाद्यकामो वा /
5.1.7.m: He should apportion [a cake] on eight potsherds to Agni, if he contends for a realm or is desirous of food.

5.1.7.d: ओजो ऽसि \\ इति हवीम्̐ष्य् आसन्नान्य् अभिमृशेत् /
5.1.7.m: He should touch the placed oblations with: "You are vigour."
With this very [mantra] he offers before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.7.s: yukṣvā hi devahūtamān iti nava dhāyyāḥ / ṣaḍ uttarā ājyabhāgahaviḥsviṣṭakṛtām /
5.1.7.d: युक्ष्वा हि देवहूतमान् इति नव धाय्याः / षड् उत्तरा आज्यभागहविःस्विष्टकृताम् /
5.1.7.m: "Harness indeed the best invoker of the gods" are the nine supplementary verses; the following six are for the clarified butter portions, the oblation, and the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

5.1.7.s: aindrābārhaspatyam̐ havir nirvaped yo rāṣṭrīyo na vijayeta /
5.1.7.d: ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यम्̐ हविर् निर्वपेद् यो राष्ट्रीयो न विजयेत /
5.1.7.m: He should apportion an oblation to Indra and Bṛhaspati, if he is an heir to a realm and does not conquer.
Having apportioned for Bṛhaspati [and] having prepared for Indra, he should proceed with both.

5.1.7.s: idam̐ vām āsye \\ iti dve haviṣaḥ /
5.1.7.d: इदम्̐ वाम् आस्ये \\ इति द्वे हविषः /
5.1.7.m: "This in the mouth of both of you" are the two [verses] for the oblation.

5.1.8.s: ādityaṃ ghṛte caruṃ nirvapen niruddham̐ yājayet /
5.1.8.d: आदित्यं घृते चरुं निर्वपेन् निरुद्धम्̐ याजयेत् /
5.1.8.m: He should apportion a boiled oblation in clarified butter to the Ādityas; he should make an expelled [king] sacrifice.
Before the Savitṛ formula he should murmur:

5.1.8.s: ādityā bhāgam̐ vaḥ kariṣyāmy amum āmuṣyāyaṇam avagamayata \\ iti niruddhasya nāma gṛhṇīyāt /
5.1.8.d: आदित्या भागम्̐ वः करिष्याम्य् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अवगमयत \\ इति निरुद्धस्य नाम गृह्णीयात् /
5.1.8.m: "O Ādityas, I will make a share for you; restore such-and-such, son of such-and-such"; he should speak the name of the expelled one.

5.1.8.s: havīm̐ṣy āsādya saptāśvatthān mayūkhān antarvedi purastāt prakṣṇutān nidadhāti /
5.1.8.d: हवीम्̐ष्य् आसाद्य सप्ताश्वत्थान् मयूखान् अन्तर्वेदि पुरस्तात् प्रक्ष्णुतान् निदधाति /
5.1.8.m: Having placed the oblations, he puts down inside the altar, in front, seven pegs of aśvattha wood, sharpened at the tip.
When [the sacrifice] is completed, he should drive them through into the middle pole of the chariot stand.

5.1.8.s: idam aham ādityān badhnāmy āmuṣyāvagamas \\ iti niruddhasya nāma gṛhṇīyāt /
5.1.8.d: इदम् अहम् आदित्यान् बध्नाम्य् आमुष्यावगमस् \\ इति निरुद्धस्य नाम गृह्णीयात् /
5.1.8.m: "Here I bind the Ādityas; let such-and-such return"; he should speak the name of the expelled one.

5.1.8.s: yadi saptāhe nāvagached idhme mayūkhān upasaṃnahyaivaṃ dviḥ saptāhe saptāhe yajeta /
5.1.8.d: यदि सप्ताहे नावगछेद् इध्मे मयूखान् उपसंनह्यैवं द्विः सप्ताहे सप्ताहे यजेत /
5.1.8.m: If he does not return in seven days, having tied the pegs to the sacrificial fuel, he should sacrifice thus every seven days for two seven-day periods.

5.1.8.s: yadi prathame nāvagached uttarābhyām iṣṭvā dhārayadvatyā yajeta /
5.1.8.d: यदि प्रथमे नावगछेद् उत्तराभ्याम् इष्ट्वा धारयद्वत्या यजेत /
5.1.8.m: If he does not return at the first, having sacrificed with the following two, he should sacrifice with the Dhārayadvatī [verse].

5.1.8.s: yadi dvitīya uttarayā yajeta / yady uttame 'ntato dhārayadvatyā /
5.1.8.d: यदि द्वितीय उत्तरया यजेत / यद्य् उत्तमे ऽन्ततो धारयद्वत्या /
5.1.8.m: If at the second, he should sacrifice with the following; if at the last, with the Dhārayadvatī at the end.

5.1.8.s: dārśapaurṇamāsika idhme mayūkhān upasaṃnahyāpi vā \\ adite 'numanyasva \ satyāśīr iha manas \\ iti niruddhasya dakṣiṇāt padāt pām̐sūn apādadīta / tadyaḥ purastādgrāmyavādīva syāttasminsabhāyāmupapiṣṭe 'bhivātaṃ pām̐sūndhvam̐sayeyuḥ preta marutaḥ svatavasa enā viśpatyāmum̐ rājānamabhīti /
5.1.8.d: दार्शपौर्णमासिक इध्मे मयूखान् उपसंनह्यापि वा \\ अदिते ऽनुमन्यस्व \ सत्याशीर् इह मनस् \\ इति निरुद्धस्य दक्षिणात् पदात् पाम्̐सून् अपाददीत / तद्यः पुरस्ताद्ग्राम्यवादीव स्यात्तस्मिन्सभायामुपपिष्टे ऽभिवातं पाम्̐सून्ध्वम्̐सयेयुः प्रेत मरुतः स्वतवस एना विश्पत्यामुम्̐ राजानमभीति /
5.1.8.m: Having tied the pegs to the sacrificial fuel of the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, or rather: with "O Aditi, consent," "True is the wish, here the mind," he should take dust from the right foot of the expelled one. Then, whoever is like a village-pleader ahead of him—when he is crushed in the assembly, they should scatter the dust toward the wind with: "Go forth, Maruts of independent might, unto this people, unto such-and-such king."

5.1.8.s: grāmyavādino gṛhād vrīhīn āhṛtya tredhā tān vicinuyād ye kṛṣṇās tān kṛṣṇājina upanahya nidadhyād ye śuklās tam ādityaṃ ghṛte caruṃ nirvapet /
5.1.8.d: ग्राम्यवादिनो गृहाद् व्रीहीन् आहृत्य त्रेधा तान् विचिनुयाद् ये कृष्णास् तान् कृष्णाजिन उपनह्य निदध्याद् ये शुक्लास् तम् आदित्यं घृते चरुं निर्वपेत् /
5.1.8.m: Having brought rice from the house of the village-pleader, he should divide it into three: those that are black, he should tie up in a black antelope skin and put aside; those that are white, he should apportion as that boiled oblation in clarified butter to the Ādityas.

5.1.8.s: ādityam̐ sam̐sthāpya yebhyo 'dhi vicinuyāt tān udaṅ paretya valmīkavapām udrujya yad adya te ghora āsan \\ iti juhoti /
5.1.8.d: आदित्यम्̐ सम्̐स्थाप्य येभ्यो ऽधि विचिनुयात् तान् उदङ् परेत्य वल्मीकवपाम् उद्रुज्य यद् अद्य ते घोर आसन् \\ इति जुहोति /
5.1.8.m: Having completed the [offering to the] Ādityas, having gone north with those from which he separated [the white grains], having broken open the moist earth of an anthill, he offers with: "What terrible [poison] was in your mouth today."
Having returned, he should sacrifice with the offering to Varuṇa, [and] with the Dhārayadvatī at the end.

5.1.8.s: tāsām ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi te \\ imam̐ yajñam iti hūtavantāv ājyabhāgau //
5.1.8.d: तासाम् एह्य् ऊ षु ब्रवाणि ते \\ इमम्̐ यज्ञम् इति हूतवन्ताव् आज्यभागौ //
5.1.8.m: For these [offerings], "Come well, let me speak to you" [and] "This sacrifice" are the two clarified butter portions containing an invitation.

5.1.8.s: tyān nu kṣatriyān \ yebhyo mātā \\ iti haviṣaḥ /
5.1.8.d: त्यान् नु क्षत्रियान् \ येभ्यो माता \\ इति हविषः /
5.1.8.m: "Those kṣatriyas now" [and] "To whom the mother" are the two [verses] for the oblation.
In the Dhārayadvatī [offering], the ritual procedure is the Vārtraghna.
"The Ādityas maintain" are the two [verses] for the oblation.

5.1.9.s: sauryaṃ ghṛte caruṃ nirvapec chuklānām̐ vrīhīṇāṃ brahmavarcasakāmaḥ /
5.1.9.d: सौर्यं घृते चरुं निर्वपेच् छुक्लानाम्̐ व्रीहीणां ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः /
5.1.9.m: Desirous of spiritual brilliance, he should apportion a boiled oblation of white rice in clarified butter to Sūrya.

5.1.9.s: udvāsayañ śātamānikau rukmau rājatam adhastāt kuryād dharitam upariṣṭāt /
5.1.9.d: उद्वासयञ् शातमानिकौ रुक्मौ राजतम् अधस्तात् कुर्याद् धरितम् उपरिष्टात् /
5.1.9.m: Taking it off the fire, he should put two hundred-māna gold plates, a silver one underneath and a golden one above.

5.1.9.s: prayājeprayāje triyavaṃ kṛṣṇalaṃ juhoti /
5.1.9.d: प्रयाजेप्रयाजे त्रियवं कृष्णलं जुहोति /
5.1.9.m: At each fore-offering he offers a three-barleycorn piece of gold.

5.1.9.s: saumāraudraṃ tantram //
5.1.9.d: सौमारौद्रं तन्त्रम् //

5.1.9.s: tat sūryasya \ bhadrā aśvās \\ iti haviṣaḥ /
5.1.9.d: तत् सूर्यस्य \ भद्रा अश्वास् \\ इति हविषः /
5.1.9.m: "That of Sūrya" [and] "Auspicious are the horses" are the two [verses] for the oblation.

5.1.9.s: śatakṛṣṇalāyāṃ catvāricatvāri kṛṣṇalāny avadānam ekaṃ prāśitram ekam avāntareḍā /
5.1.9.d: शतकृष्णलायां चत्वारिचत्वारि कृष्णलान्य् अवदानम् एकं प्राशित्रम् एकम् अवान्तरेडा /
5.1.9.m: In the [offering] of a hundred pieces of gold, the cutting consists of four pieces of gold each: one is the priest's portion, one the intermediate iḍā.

5.1.9.s: caruṃ brahmaṇe pariharati /
5.1.9.d: चरुं ब्रह्मणे परिहरति /
5.1.9.m: He hands the boiled oblation around to the brahman priest.

5.1.9.s: niścūṣya bhakṣān upayachanti /
5.1.9.d: निश्चूष्य भक्षान् उपयछन्ति /
5.1.9.m: Having sucked them clean, they hold the consumable portions.

5.1.9.s: jīvitavān kalpaḥ //
5.1.9.d: जीवितवान् कल्पः //

5.1.9.s: hiraṇyagarbhas \\ yaḥ prāṇatas \\ iti haviṣaḥ /
5.1.9.d: हिरण्यगर्भस् \\ यः प्राणतस् \\ इति हविषः /
5.1.9.m: "The Golden Germ" [and] "Who by his breath" are the two [verses] for the oblation.

5.1.9.s: bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvapet purodhākāmaḥ /
5.1.9.d: बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं निर्वपेत् पुरोधाकामः /
5.1.9.m: Desirous of the office of domestic priest, he should apportion a boiled oblation to Bṛhaspati.

5.1.9.s: tasyā grāmakāmaṃ tantram /
5.1.9.d: तस्या ग्रामकामं तन्त्रम् /
5.1.9.m: Its ritual framework is that for one desiring a village.

5.1.9.s: aindrābārhaspatyasyāmnāte /
5.1.9.d: ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यस्याम्नाते /
5.1.9.m: Those of the [offering] to Indra and Bṛhaspati are traditionally handed down [as the verses].

5.1.9.s: bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvapet payasi grāmakāmaḥ paśukāmo vā /
5.1.9.d: बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं निर्वपेत् पयसि ग्रामकामः पशुकामो वा /
5.1.9.m: Desirous of a village or desirous of cattle, he should apportion a boiled oblation in milk to Bṛhaspati.

5.1.9.s: bahupuṣṭasya gṛhāt kṣīram āhṛtya svāsāṃ ca gavāṃ praṇītodakena sam̐sṛjya carum̐ śrapayati /
5.1.9.d: बहुपुष्टस्य गृहात् क्षीरम् आहृत्य स्वासां च गवां प्रणीतोदकेन सम्̐सृज्य चरुम्̐ श्रपयति /
5.1.9.m: Having brought milk from the house of a prosperous man and from his own cows, having mixed it with the brought-forward water, he cooks the boiled oblation.

5.1.9.s: brāhmaṇaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvapet saṃgrāmaṃ jigīṣan senayoḥ saṃdṛśyamānayoḥ /
5.1.9.d: ब्राह्मणस्पत्यं चरुं निर्वपेत् संग्रामं जिगीषन् सेनयोः संदृश्यमानयोः /
5.1.9.m: Wishing to win a battle when two armies are in sight of each other, he should apportion a boiled oblation to Brahmaṇaspati.

5.1.9.s: udbarhiḥ prastara iṣuṇāṃ bāṇavantaḥ paridhayaḥ pattrato mūlāni /
5.1.9.d: उद्बर्हिः प्रस्तर इषुणां बाणवन्तः परिधयः पत्त्रतो मूलानि /
5.1.9.m: The sacred grass bundle is pulled up; the enclosing sticks are arrows possessing reed-shafts, their bases by the feathering.

5.1.9.s: prastaram anupraharan pātryām upādadhīta /
5.1.9.d: प्रस्तरम् अनुप्रहरन् पात्र्याम् उपादधीत /
5.1.9.m: Throwing the sacred grass bundle after [the oblation], he should place it upon the vessel.

5.1.9.s: brāhmaṇaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvaped yatra kāmayeta brahmabalam̐ syād iti //
5.1.9.d: ब्राह्मणस्पत्यं चरुं निर्वपेद् यत्र कामयेत ब्रह्मबलम्̐ स्याद् इति //
5.1.9.m: He should apportion a boiled oblation to Brahmaṇaspati where he wishes: 'May there be the power of the brahman.'

5.1.9.s: bṛhaspatiḥ prathamaṃ jāyamānas \\ ity aṣṭau haviṣām /
5.1.9.d: बृहस्पतिः प्रथमं जायमानस् \\ इत्य् अष्टौ हविषाम् /
5.1.9.m: "Bṛhaspati, being born first" are the eight [verses] for the oblations.

5.1.9.s: na bṛhatyā vaṣaṭkaroti /
5.1.9.d: न बृहत्या वषट्करोति /
5.1.9.m: He does not utter the vaṣaṭ-call with a bṛhatī verse.

5.1.9.s: anuvākyāyāścatvāryakṣarāṇi yājyāmabhyatyūhati /
5.1.9.d: अनुवाक्यायाश्चत्वार्यक्षराणि याज्यामभ्यत्यूहति /
5.1.9.m: He shifts four syllables of the invitatory verse over into the offering verse.

5.1.9.s:
uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate \ devayantas tvemahe /
upa prayantu marutaḥ sudānavās \ indra prāśom //
ity anvāha // bhavā sacā \\ agnir ukthe \\ iti yaja /
5.1.9.d:
उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पते \ देवयन्तस् त्वेमहे /
उप प्रयन्तु मरुतः सुदानवास् \ इन्द्र प्राशोम् //
इत्य् अन्वाह // भवा सचा \\ अग्निर् उक्थे \\ इति यज /
5.1.9.m:
“Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati, seeking the gods we implore you...”

“Let the bountiful Maruts advance, Indra drink the offering...”

thus he recites. “Be our companion...”, “Agni in praise...”: recite the offering verse with these.

5.1.9.s: gārmute bṛhaspate juṣasva nas \\ evā pitre \\ iti bārhaspatyasya / saumāpauṣṇasyāmnāte /
5.1.9.d: गार्मुते बृहस्पते जुषस्व नस् \\ एवा पित्रे \\ इति बार्हस्पत्यस्य / सौमापौष्णस्याम्नाते /
5.1.9.m: For the Gārmuta offering: “O Bṛhaspati, take pleasure in us...”, “Thus to the father...”—these are for that belonging to Bṛhaspati. Those of the offering to Soma and Pūṣan are traditionally taught.

5.1.9.s: prājāpatyam adhiśritya prāk paryagnikaraṇād gārmute gomūtrasyāścotayet /
5.1.9.d: प्राजापत्यम् अधिश्रित्य प्राक् पर्यग्निकरणाद् गार्मुते गोमूत्रस्याश्चोतयेत् /
5.1.9.m: Having placed [the oblation] for Prajāpati on the fire, before the carrying of fire around it, he should sprinkle cow's urine into the Gārmuta oblation.

5.1.9.s: vāstvamayaḥ kaṇikaḥ /
5.1.9.d: वास्त्वमयः कणिकः /

5.1.9.s: prāyaścittiḥ kalpaḥ //
5.1.9.d: प्रायश्चित्तिः कल्पः //

5.1.9.s: namas te rudra manyave \\ imā rudrāya \\ iti haviṣaḥ /
5.1.9.d: नमस् ते रुद्र मन्यवे \\ इमा रुद्राय \\ इति हविषः /
5.1.9.m: “Homage to your wrath, O Rudra...”, “These to Rudra...”—these are for the oblation.

5.1.9.s: niṣādasthapater iṣṭiḥ /
5.1.9.d: निषादस्थपतेर् इष्टिः /
5.1.9.m: [This is] the sacrifice of a Niṣāda chieftain.

5.1.9.s: āmnātā dakṣiṇā /
5.1.9.d: आम्नाता दक्षिणा /

5.1.9.s: rājā parameṣṭhikāmaḥ parameṣṭhine dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet /
5.1.9.d: राजा परमेष्ठिकामः परमेष्ठिने द्वादशकपालं निर्वपेत् /
5.1.9.m: A king desiring the highest station should apportion a twelve-potsherd [cake] to Parameṣṭhin.

5.1.9.s: prāk sviṣṭakṛto 'dhijyaṃ dhanus tisraś ceṣūr agniṣ ṭe tejas \\ iti yajamānāya prayachati / sā dakṣiṇā /
5.1.9.d: प्राक् स्विष्टकृतो ऽधिज्यं धनुस् तिस्रश् चेषूर् अग्निष् टे तेजस् \\ इति यजमानाय प्रयछति / सा दक्षिणा /
5.1.9.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he hands over to the sacrificer a strung bow and three arrows with: “May Agni [grant] you splendor...”. That is the sacrificial gift.

5.1.9.s: vaiśvadevaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvaped bhrātṛvyavān /
5.1.9.d: वैश्वदेवं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपेद् भ्रातृव्यवान् /
5.1.9.m: One who has a rival should apportion a twelve-potsherd [cake] to the Viśve Devas.

5.1.9.s: ājyabhāgābhyāṃ pracarya barhiṣi puroḍāśaṃ nidhāya sphyena \\ idam ahaṃ māṃ cāmuṃ ca vyūhāmi \\ iti yaṃ dviṣyāt tasya nāma gṛhṇīyād barhiṣy avasannam̐ sphye ca śliṣṭaṃ tad viṣṇava urukramāyāvadyet /
5.1.9.d: आज्यभागाभ्यां प्रचर्य बर्हिषि पुरोडाशं निधाय स्फ्येन \\ इदम् अहं मां चामुं च व्यूहामि \\ इति यं द्विष्यात् तस्य नाम गृह्णीयाद् बर्हिष्य् अवसन्नम्̐ स्फ्ये च श्लिष्टं तद् विष्णव उरुक्रमायावद्येत् /
